title: GLBA Regulation P initial privacy notice at customer relationship inception
requirement: A financial institution must deliver a clear and conspicuous initial notice of its privacy policies and practices to each customer not later than when it establishes a customer relationship, and to a consumer before disclosing that consumer's nonpublic personal information to a nonaffiliated third party. Applies to the enterprise's non-insurance financial affiliates/functions under CFPB jurisdiction; the insurance-underwriting entity itself is functionally regulated by state insurance authorities under NAIC #672.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 12 CFR Part 1016 (Regulation P), CFPB; Reg P restated GLBA Title V privacy rule, current as of 2026.

title: GLBA Regulation P opt-out notice before sharing NPI with nonaffiliated third parties
requirement: Before disclosing a consumer's nonpublic personal information to a nonaffiliated third party outside the §§1016.13-15 exceptions, a financial institution must give a clear and conspicuous opt-out notice explaining the right to opt out and a reasonable means to exercise it, and honor opt-out elections. Applies to CFPB-regulated financial affiliates; state DOI (NAIC #672) governs the insurance entity.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 12 CFR 1016.7 and 1016.10, CFPB Regulation P; current 2026.

title: GLBA Regulation P annual privacy notice (unless FAST Act exception met)
requirement: A financial institution must provide a clear and conspicuous privacy notice to customers at least once in any period of 12 consecutive months during which the relationship continues, unless it qualifies for the FAST Act exception (shares NPI only within §§1016.13-15 and has not changed disclosed policies). Applies to CFPB-regulated financial affiliates.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 12 CFR 1016.5; FAST Act §75001 (Dec 4, 2015) annual-notice exception implemented by 2018 CFPB amendment.

title: FTC Safeguards Rule written information security program with qualified individual
requirement: Non-bank financial institutions under FTC jurisdiction (e.g., the enterprise's insurance agencies, premium-finance and other financial arms not otherwise functionally regulated) must develop, implement and maintain a comprehensive written information security program with a designated qualified individual, risk assessment, access controls, encryption, MFA, monitoring and vendor oversight. The insurance underwriter itself is exempt where regulated by a state insurance authority under GLBA §505.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 16 CFR Part 314; 2021 amendments phased in, program-element compliance date June 9, 2023; current 2026.

title: FTC Safeguards Rule notify FTC of security breach affecting 500+ consumers within 30 days
requirement: A covered non-bank financial institution must notify the FTC as soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after discovery, of a security event involving unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers, via the FTC's online reporting portal. Applies to FTC-jurisdiction financial affiliates, not the state-regulated insurer.
sourceNote: Verified FTC final rule (Fed. Reg. Nov 13, 2023); breach-notification requirement effective May 13, 2024.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services, Office for Civil Rights
title: HIPAA maintain and distribute Notice of Privacy Practices for health plan
requirement: A health plan (covered entity) must maintain a Notice of Privacy Practices describing PHI uses/disclosures and individual rights, provide it to new enrollees, notify members of its availability at least once every three years, and distribute revised notices after material changes. Updated NPP addressing reproductive-health provisions must be in place by the Feb 16, 2026 compliance date.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 45 CFR 164.520; 2024 reproductive-health final rule NPP amendments, compliance date Feb 16, 2026 (some 164.520(b) provisions vacated June 2025).

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services, Office for Civil Rights
title: HIPAA safeguard PHI and limit uses/disclosures to minimum necessary
requirement: A health plan covered entity must not use or disclose protected health information except as permitted by the Privacy Rule, apply the minimum-necessary standard, obtain valid authorizations where required (including new attestations for certain reproductive-health disclosures), and honor individuals' rights of access, amendment and accounting of disclosures.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E (Privacy); minimum-necessary and authorization standards current 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services, Office for Civil Rights
title: HIPAA Security Rule safeguards and annual risk analysis for ePHI
requirement: A health plan covered entity must implement administrative, physical and technical safeguards for electronic PHI, including conducting an accurate and thorough risk analysis of confidentiality/integrity/availability risks, a risk-management process, workforce security, contingency planning and access controls. Applies to the health line's ePHI systems.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 45 CFR 164.308 (Security Rule administrative safeguards); OCR NPRM to strengthen Security Rule pending (published Jan 6, 2025).

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services, Office for Civil Rights
title: HIPAA notify individuals of PHI breach within 60 days of discovery
requirement: Following discovery of a breach of unsecured protected health information, a health plan covered entity must notify each affected individual without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery, including a description of the breach, information involved, protective steps, and mitigation actions.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 45 CFR 164.404 (Breach Notification Rule); current 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services, Office for Civil Rights
title: HIPAA report breach affecting 500+ individuals to HHS Secretary within 60 days
requirement: For a breach of unsecured PHI affecting 500 or more individuals, a health plan covered entity must notify the HHS Secretary contemporaneously with individual notice and no later than 60 days after discovery, via the OCR breach portal, and must notify prominent media serving any state/jurisdiction where 500+ residents are affected.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 45 CFR 164.408 and 164.406; HHS breach portal reporting current 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services, Office for Civil Rights
title: HIPAA annual submission of breaches affecting fewer than 500 individuals
requirement: For breaches of unsecured PHI affecting fewer than 500 individuals, a health plan covered entity must maintain a log and submit these breaches to the HHS Secretary via the OCR portal no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar year in which they were discovered.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 45 CFR 164.408(c); annual small-breach filing due within 60 days of year end, current 2026.

title: TCPA obtain prior express written consent for autodialed/prerecorded telemarketing
requirement: Before initiating a telemarketing call or text to a wireless number (or a prerecorded-voice telemarketing call to a residential line) using an automatic telephone dialing system or artificial/prerecorded voice, the carrier must obtain the called party's prior express written consent: a signed written agreement clearly authorizing such messages, disclosing that consent is not a condition of purchase.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR/Cornell 47 CFR 64.1200(a)(2), (f)(9); one-to-one consent variant vacated by 11th Cir. Jan 2025 and removed by FCC Sept 2025 final rule.

title: TCPA scrub telemarketing calls against the National Do-Not-Call Registry
requirement: The carrier must not make telemarketing calls to residential/wireless numbers on the National Do-Not-Call Registry, using a version of the registry obtained from the administrator no more than 31 days before any call, and must maintain records documenting its DNC compliance process and access to the registry.
sourceNote: Verified 47 CFR 64.1200(c)(2)(i)(D); 31-day registry-refresh requirement current 2026.

title: TCPA maintain internal do-not-call list and written DNC policy
requirement: The carrier must maintain a written policy (available on demand) for an internal/company-specific do-not-call list, train telemarketing personnel, record consumer do-not-call requests at the time made, and honor them within a reasonable time not exceeding 10 business days from receipt.
sourceNote: Verified 47 CFR 64.1200(d)(1)-(3); internal DNC and 10-business-day honoring current 2026.

title: TCPA honor consent revocation by any reasonable means within 10 business days
requirement: The carrier must treat a consumer's use of any reasonable method (including keywords stop, quit, end, revoke, opt out, cancel, unsubscribe) as revocation of prior express consent for calls/texts, process the revocation within a reasonable time not to exceed 10 business days, and cease further messages. (The broader revoke-all provision is delayed to Jan 2027.)
sourceNote: Verified FCC order; core revocation rule 47 CFR 64.1200(a)(10) effective April 11, 2025; revoke-all portion extended to Jan 2027.

title: CAN-SPAM commercial email: functioning opt-out and honor within 10 business days
requirement: Each commercial email the carrier sends must include a clear opt-out mechanism (reply email or single web page) that stays functional at least 30 days after sending; the carrier must honor opt-out requests within 10 business days and may not require any information beyond an email address or any step beyond a reply/single page to unsubscribe.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 16 CFR Part 316 and FTC CAN-SPAM compliance guide; 10-business-day opt-out and 30-day mechanism current 2026.

title: CAN-SPAM header, subject-line accuracy and physical postal address disclosure
requirement: Each commercial email must have accurate, non-deceptive header/from information and subject lines, identify the message as an advertisement, and include the sender's valid physical postal address. These content requirements apply to all marketing emails the carrier sends.
sourceNote: Verified FTC CAN-SPAM compliance guide and 15 U.S.C. 7704(a); current 2026.

title: FCRA adverse action notice when insurance decision uses a consumer report
requirement: When the carrier takes an adverse action on an insurance application/policy (denial, increased premium, less favorable terms) based in whole or in part on a consumer report, it must provide an adverse action notice identifying the consumer reporting agency (name, address, toll-free number), stating the CRA did not make the decision, and informing the consumer of the right to a free file disclosure within 60 days and to dispute inaccuracies.
sourceNote: Verified 15 U.S.C. 1681m(a) (FCRA §615(a)); insurance is a covered adverse-action context, current 2026.

title: FCRA credit-based insurance score disclosure with adverse action notice
requirement: When a credit-based insurance score derived from a consumer report is used in taking adverse action, the carrier must disclose the numerical score, the range, key factors adversely affecting the score, the score date, and the CRA that provided it, in addition to the general adverse action notice.
sourceNote: Verified FCRA §§615(a)/609(f) score-disclosure duty via FTC guidance and 15 U.S.C. 1681m; current 2026.

title: FCRA prescreen firm-offer opt-out notice on marketed insurance solicitations
requirement: When the carrier uses prescreened consumer report information to make a firm offer of insurance not initiated by the consumer, each written solicitation must contain a clear and conspicuous short-form and long-form opt-out notice (per FCRA §615(d)) informing consumers of the right to opt out of prescreened offers and the toll-free number (1-888-5-OPT-OUT) to do so.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 12 CFR 1022.54 (Reg V prescreen opt-out) and 15 U.S.C. 1681m(d); current 2026.

title: FCRA obtain consumer reports only for a permissible purpose (insurance underwriting)
requirement: The carrier may obtain a consumer report only for a permissible purpose enumerated in FCRA §604 - for underwriting/rating insurance in connection with a transaction involving the consumer, or a firm offer of insurance - and must certify the permissible purpose to the consumer reporting agency and use the report only for that purpose.
sourceNote: Verified 15 U.S.C. 1681b(a)(3) permissible-purpose (insurance underwriting); current 2026.

title: FTC Health Breach Notification for non-HIPAA consumer health apps/PHRs
requirement: If the carrier offers a vendor-of-personal-health-records or health-app product that draws PHR-identifiable health information and is NOT covered by HIPAA, then following a breach of security it must notify affected individuals, the FTC, and (for 500+ individuals) the media, without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery.
sourceNote: Verified eCFR 16 CFR Part 318; 2024 amendments (expanded health-app scope) effective July 29, 2024. Applies only if carrier operates a non-HIPAA PHR/app.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
title: Sanctions/SDN List Screening of Policyholders, Insureds, Beneficiaries & Claimants
requirement: As a U.S. person, the carrier must screen applicants, policyholders, insureds, additional insureds, beneficiaries, claimants and payees against OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List and other sanctions lists before binding coverage, paying premiums/commissions, or settling claims. Screening must follow a risk-based program aligned with OFAC's Framework for Compliance Commitments; providing insurance or paying a claim to a blocked person absent a license is a strict-liability violation.
citation: 31 CFR Chapter V (OFAC sanctions regulations); OFAC Insurance Industry FAQs (topic 1616)
sourceNote: Verified on ofac.treasury.gov Insurance Industry FAQs; industry-specific FAQs updated 13 Nov 2024 (Morgan Lewis, Crowell alerts confirm). Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
title: Block Newly-Sanctioned Policy & Report Blocking to OFAC Within 10 Business Days
requirement: When an existing policyholder, insured or named beneficiary becomes blocked (or a transaction must be blocked) and no license/exemption applies, the carrier must block the policy or the relevant portion, place future premium payments into a blocked interest-bearing U.S. account, and report the blocking to OFAC within 10 business days via the OFAC Reporting System. A separate specific license is required to pay any otherwise-prohibited claim.
sourceNote: Verified via OFAC Insurance FAQs (updated 13 Nov 2024) and 31 CFR 501.603 (Reporting, Procedures and Penalties Regulations). 10-business-day rule current as of 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
title: Annual Report of Blocked Property (TD F 90-22.50) to OFAC by September 30
requirement: Any person holding property blocked under OFAC sanctions as of June 30 must file the Annual Report of Blocked Property (ARBP) using spreadsheet form TD F 90-22.50 through the OFAC Reporting System no later than September 30 each year. For insurers this captures blocked policies, blocked premium/claim funds and blocked accounts. Failure to file by the deadline is itself a violation.
sourceNote: Verified via 31 CFR 501.603(b) and OFAC ARBP guidance/form TD F 90-22.50 (ofac.treasury.gov). June 30 hold date, Sept 30 due date current as of 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN)
regime: Bank Secrecy Act - Insurance Company AML Rules (31 CFR Part 1025)
title: Establish & Maintain a BSA/AML Program for Covered Insurance Products
requirement: An insurance company that issues or underwrites 'covered products' (permanent (non-group) life insurance, non-group annuity contracts, and any other insurance product with cash value or investment features) must develop and implement a written, risk-based AML program reasonably designed to prevent it from being used to launder money or finance terrorism. The program must include policies/procedures/controls, a designated compliance officer, ongoing employee training, and independent testing.
sourceNote: Verified via eCFR 31 CFR 1025.210 and FinCEN insurance AML FAQs. Covered-product scope confirmed on fincen.gov. Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN)
regime: Bank Secrecy Act - Insurance Company AML Rules (31 CFR Part 1025)
title: File Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) on Covered Insurance Products
requirement: An insurance company must file a SAR with FinCEN for any transaction involving a covered product that aggregates at least $5,000 in funds or assets where the company knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect the transaction involves illicit funds, is structured to evade BSA requirements, has no lawful business purpose, or facilitates criminal activity. The SAR must be filed within 30 days of initial detection (up to 60 if identifying a suspect) and supporting records kept 5 years.
sourceNote: Verified via 31 CFR 1025.320 (law.cornell.edu): $5,000 threshold, 30/60-day filing, 5-year record retention. Current as of 2026.

title: Report Cash Receipts Over $10,000 on Form 8300
requirement: A carrier that in the course of its trade or business receives more than $10,000 in cash (or specified cash equivalents) in one transaction or two or more related transactions must file Form 8300 with the IRS/FinCEN by the 15th day after receipt and furnish an annual statement to the payer. Payments for policies/annuities made by check/wire generally do not trigger it, but cash premiums, cash restitution, and similar cash receipts do.
sourceNote: Verified via IRS Form 8300 insurance-industry guidance and Form 8300 (Rev. Dec 2023) instructions. 15-day filing rule current as of 2026.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Federal Insurance Office (Terrorism Risk Insurance Program)
title: Mandatory Annual TRIP Terrorism Risk Insurance Data Call to Treasury
requirement: Every insurer writing commercial property/casualty lines subject to the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program must register on the TRIP data-collection portal and submit the OMB-approved data-call forms each year (subject to small-insurer/captive exemptions). The 2026 data call covers the Jan 1-Dec 31 2025 reporting period with completed forms due no later than May 15, 2026.
citation: Terrorism Risk Insurance Act of 2002 (as amended) sec. 104; 31 CFR Part 50
sourceNote: Verified via Treasury TRIP Annual Data Collection page and Federal Register notice 2026-05794 (25 Mar 2026): mandatory, May 15 2026 deadline, 2025 reporting year.

regulatorName: Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) - National Flood Insurance Program
title: WYO Flood Policy/Claim Reporting to FEMA under the TRRP Plan
requirement: A carrier participating as an NFIP Write-Your-Own company must record and report all flood policy and claims transactions to the NFIP Bureau and Statistical Agent in accordance with the WYO Transaction Record Reporting and Processing (TRRP) Plan, the WYO Accounting Procedures Manual, and the WYO Financial Control Plan, and must comply with these requirements as a condition of the annual WYO Arrangement (monthly transaction submissions and reconciliations).
sourceNote: Verified via eCFR 44 CFR 62.23 and FEMA WYO Financial Control Plan (Jan 2026) + consolidated TRRP Plan on agents.floodsmart.gov. Current as of 2026.

title: Annual Form 1099-R Reporting of Annuity & Insurance-Contract Distributions
requirement: The carrier must file Form 1099-R with the IRS and furnish a copy to each recipient for every designated distribution of $10 or more from annuities, pensions, insurance contracts, charitable gift annuities, and disability payments under life contracts. Recipient statements are due by January 31 and IRS filing (electronic if 10+ returns) is due by March 31 (Feb 28 if on paper) following the calendar year.
sourceNote: Verified via 2026 IRS Instructions for Forms 1099-R and 5498 (irs.gov): $10 threshold, Jan 31 recipient / March 31 e-file deadlines. Current as of 2026.

regime: Affordable Care Act - Section 6055 MEC Reporting
title: Annual Minimum Essential Coverage Reporting via Forms 1094-B/1095-B
requirement: As a health insurance issuer providing minimum essential coverage, the carrier must report each covered individual's coverage to the IRS on Forms 1095-B with transmittal Form 1094-B, and furnish (or make available on request under the alternative-notice method) a statement to each responsible individual. For the 2025 tax year, statements are due by March 2, 2026 and IRS filing (electronic if 10+ returns) by March 31, 2026.
sourceNote: Verified via IRS Section 6055 Q&A (irs.gov): issuers file 1094-B/1095-B; 2025 tax-year furnishing due Mar 2, 2026, e-file due Mar 31, 2026.

title: Section 111 NGHP Medicare Secondary Payer reporting (liability/no-fault/WC) via BCRC
requirement: As a Responsible Reporting Entity for liability (including self-insurance), no-fault, and workers' compensation, the carrier must report to CMS ORM assumption and TPOC settlement/judgment/award data on Medicare beneficiaries so Medicare can coordinate benefits. Reporting is electronic and submitted on the RRE's assigned quarterly file submission schedule; noncompliance triggers civil money penalties. Pass condition is accepted quarterly ORM/TPOC records within CMS thresholds.
sourceNote: Verified on CMS Mandatory Insurer Reporting (NGHP) page; NGHP User Guide v8.4 current, quarterly CMS compliance audits begin April 1, 2026 (250 records/quarter).

title: Section 111 GHP Medicare Secondary Payer coverage reporting via BCRC
requirement: As an insurer or TPA for a group health plan (and, for self-insured/self-administered plans, the plan administrator or fiduciary), the carrier must report active covered-life/coverage data on Medicare beneficiaries so Medicare can determine primary vs. secondary payer status. Reporting is done quarterly in the CMS-specified electronic format; the RRE remains solely accountable for data accuracy even when using an agent. Pass condition is accepted quarterly GHP coverage records.
sourceNote: Verified on CMS Mandatory Insurer Reporting for GHP page; GHP User Guide v7.7 issued January 5, 2026, quarterly electronic reporting.

regulatorName: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services / HHS
title: Annual MLR report submission to HHS by June 1 via CMS MLR Annual Reporting Form
requirement: As a health insurance issuer, the carrier must annually report to HHS its premium revenue and expenditures on clinical services, quality-improvement activities, and non-claims costs for each state and market. The MLR Annual Reporting Form must be filed no later than June 1 following the close of the MLR reporting year. Pass condition is a complete, timely filing covering all applicable market segments.
sourceNote: Verified in eCFR 45 CFR Part 158 Subpart A; June 1 filing deadline still current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services / HHS
title: MLR rebate calculation and payment to enrollees by September 30 if MLR standard not met
requirement: If the carrier's MLR is below 85% (large group) or 80% (small group/individual) for a reporting year, it must rebate the difference to enrollees. Rebates must be provided by September 30 following the MLR reporting year (per the current deadline reflected in Part 158). Pass condition is accurate rebate calculation and full, timely disbursement to the correct enrollees/policyholders.
sourceNote: Verified in eCFR 45 CFR 158.240; rebate obligation triggered when applicable MLR standard is not met.

regulatorName: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services / HHS
title: Annual MLR/rebate notice to enrollees under 45 CFR 158.251
requirement: The carrier must provide each enrollee, in each market and state where it is required to pay a rebate (and in certain non-rebate cases), a notice of MLR information describing the MLR standard, the issuer's MLR, and any rebate. The notice must accompany the rebate or be provided with the first plan document following the reporting year. Pass condition is delivery of the compliant notice to all applicable enrollees.
sourceNote: Verified via LII/eCFR 45 CFR 158.251 (Notice of MLR information); current.

title: QPA disclosure with initial payment or denial notice to out-of-network providers
requirement: For each out-of-network item/service subject to surprise-billing protections, the plan/issuer must disclose the Qualifying Payment Amount to the provider at the time of the initial payment or notice of denial, along with a statement that the QPA equals the recognized amount and was calculated per the regulatory methodology, plus disclosure of any downcoding. The QPA must be computed as the median contracted rate, separately by provider specialty. Pass condition is a compliant QPA disclosure on each qualifying claim.
sourceNote: Verified via Requirements Related to Surprise Billing final rule (Fed. Reg. 2022-18202) and CMS No Surprises resources; QPA methodology and disclosure in force.

title: Federal IDR registry enrollment and unique registration number on payment notices
requirement: Under the Federal IDR Operations final rule, the plan/issuer must register with the Departments to obtain a unique IDR registration number, and must include on each initial payment or denial notice its legal business name, the plan sponsor's legal business name, and its IDR registration number. This addresses plan-identification friction in the IDR process. Pass condition is active registration plus complete identifiers on qualifying notices.
sourceNote: Verified via Federal IDR Operations final rule published in Federal Register June 4, 2026 (finalized May 28, 2026); new registration-number disclosure requirement.

title: Participation in Federal Independent Dispute Resolution for out-of-network payment disputes
requirement: When open negotiation over an out-of-network payment fails, the plan/issuer must participate in the Federal IDR process, submitting its offer and permitted information to the certified IDR entity, which selects one party's offer under baseball-style arbitration. The plan must pay the determined amount within the required timeframe. Pass condition is timely, good-faith participation and payment of IDR determinations.
sourceNote: Verified via CMS Federal IDR Operations Final Rule fact sheet; process in force with 2026 operational updates.

title: Provider directory accuracy: verification process and 90-day update protocol
requirement: The plan/issuer must establish a process to verify and update its provider directory information at least every 90 days, remove providers it cannot verify, respond to enrollee inquiries about a provider's network status by phone and electronically within one business day, and honor cost-sharing/no-balance-bill protections when enrollees rely on inaccurate directory information. Pass condition is a documented, operating verification-and-response process.
sourceNote: Verified via CMS NSA training on disclosure/continuity of care/directories (PHSA 2799A-5); enforced since plan years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2022.

title: Continuity-of-care transitional coverage on provider network termination
requirement: When an in-network provider/facility contract terminates, the plan/issuer must timely notify each continuing-care patient of the termination and their right to elect continued transitional care, and must provide up to 90 days of continued in-network-level coverage for qualifying patients. Pass condition is timely notice and honoring elected transitional coverage at in-network terms.
sourceNote: Verified via CMS NSA training deck (continuity of care, PHSA 2799A-3); in effect.

title: Insurance ID cards showing deductibles, out-of-pocket max, and consumer-assistance contacts
requirement: The plan/issuer must include on any physical or electronic plan ID card the applicable deductible, the applicable out-of-pocket maximum, and a telephone number and website for consumer assistance. Pass condition is compliant ID cards issued to all participants, beneficiaries, and enrollees.
sourceNote: Verified via CMS NSA legal-citations document; ID-card requirement in effect since Jan 1, 2022.

title: Public machine-readable files: in-network rates and out-of-network allowed amounts
requirement: The plan/issuer must post and monthly update publicly available machine-readable files disclosing (1) negotiated rates for all covered items/services with in-network providers and (2) historical out-of-network allowed amounts and billed charges, in the CMS-specified format on an accessible website with no access restrictions. Pass condition is complete, current, correctly formatted files.
sourceNote: Verified in eCFR 45 CFR 147.212 (public disclosure MRFs); in-network and OON files enforced (Rx-file enforcement separately deferred).

title: Self-service cost-estimator tool disclosing personalized out-of-pocket estimates
requirement: The plan/issuer must furnish, on request from a participant/beneficiary/enrollee, personalized cost-sharing estimates for covered items/services through an internet-based self-service tool and in paper form, covering all covered items and services. Pass condition is an operational tool returning compliant estimates for the full item/service set.
sourceNote: Verified in eCFR 45 CFR 147.211 (required disclosures to enrollees); full item/service list phased in for plan years on/after Jan 1, 2024.

title: NQTL comparative analyses for mental-health/substance-use benefit parity
requirement: The plan/issuer offering MH/SUD benefits must conduct, document, and make available on request comparative analyses demonstrating that each nonquantitative treatment limitation (e.g., prior authorization, network composition, out-of-network reimbursement) is comparable and applied no more stringently to MH/SUD than to medical/surgical benefits. Pass condition is complete, content-compliant analyses furnished within the regulatory timeframe when requested.
sourceNote: 2024 final rule published Sept 23, 2024 (Fed. Reg. 2024-20612). CAUTION: Departments announced (May 15, 2025) non-enforcement of the 2024 final rule pending litigation; the underlying statutory comparative-analysis duty (CAA 2021) remains in force. Effective-date note in coverageNotes.

title: Prior-authorization decision timeframes: 72 hours expedited / 7 days standard
requirement: As an impacted payer (Medicare Advantage, state Medicaid FFS and managed care, CHIP FFS and managed care, and QHP issuers on the FFEs), the carrier must send prior-authorization decisions within 72 hours for expedited requests and 7 calendar days for standard requests, and provide a specific reason for any denial. Pass condition is meeting the decision-timeframe and denial-reason standards effective January 1, 2026.
sourceNote: Verified via CMS-0057-F fact sheet; operational PA provisions (timeframes, denial reasons) effective Jan 1, 2026.

title: Annual public reporting of aggregate prior-authorization metrics by March 31
requirement: As an impacted payer, the carrier must publicly report on its website, on an annual basis, aggregate prior-authorization metrics (e.g., percent approved, denied, and approved after appeal, and average decision time). The first report is due by March 31, 2026. Pass condition is a complete, timely annual public metrics report.
sourceNote: Verified via CMS-0057-F fact sheet and multiple 2026 implementation summaries; first metrics report due March 31, 2026.

title: Prior Authorization API (FHIR) in production by January 1, 2027
requirement: As an impacted payer, the carrier must implement and operate a FHIR-based Prior Authorization API that identifies whether PA is required, communicates PA requirements/documentation, and supports electronic PA request/response, in production by January 1, 2027. Pass condition is a conformant, operational PA API meeting the standards and implementation guides.
sourceNote: Verified via CMS-0057-F final rule materials; API compliance date January 1, 2027.

title: Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer FHIR APIs in production by January 1, 2027
requirement: As an impacted payer, the carrier must implement a Provider Access API (sharing claims, encounter, and clinical data with in-network providers) and a Payer-to-Payer API (exchanging a member's data with prior/concurrent payers on enrollment) using the required FHIR standards, in production by January 1, 2027. Pass condition is conformant, operational Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer APIs with member opt-out handling.
sourceNote: Verified via CMS-0057-F final rule materials; Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer API compliance date January 1, 2027.

title: Patient Access API expansion to include prior-authorization data by January 1, 2027
requirement: As an impacted payer, the carrier must enhance its existing Patient Access API to include prior-authorization request/decision information (excluding drugs) and must annually report Patient Access API usage metrics to CMS, in production by January 1, 2027. Pass condition is a conformant Patient Access API including PA data plus the annual usage-metric report to CMS.
sourceNote: Verified via CMS-0057-F final rule materials; Patient Access API PA-data expansion compliance date January 1, 2027, with annual metrics reporting to CMS.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
title: Initial Report of Blocked Property to OFAC within 10 business days of blocking
requirement: When an insurer blocks a policy, premium, claim payment or other property because a policyholder, insured or beneficiary is a sanctioned/SDN party (and no license or exemption applies), it must file an initial report of the blocked property to OFAC. The report is due within 10 business days from the date the property becomes blocked and must be filed through the OFAC Reporting System (ORS).
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR/Cornell text of 31 CFR 501.603 and OFAC insurance-industry FAQs (topic 1616); standing requirement, reaffirmed by OFAC insurer FAQs updated Nov 2024.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
title: Annual Report of Blocked Property (ARBP) to OFAC by September 30
requirement: An insurer holding any property still blocked as of June 30 must file an Annual Report of Blocked Property (ARBP) with OFAC by September 30 of the same year, itemizing all blocked assets. Filing uses spreadsheet form TD-F 90-22.50 submitted through the OFAC Reporting System.
sourceNote: Verified against eCFR/Cornell 31 CFR 501.603 and OFAC 'Reminder to File the 2026 Annual Report of Blocked Property' (recent-actions, July 2026); annual, property held as of June 30 due Sept 30.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN)
title: Maintain risk-based AML compliance program for covered life/annuity products
requirement: An insurance company that issues or underwrites a 'covered product' (permanent life insurance other than group, annuity contracts other than group, and any insurance product with cash value or investment features) must develop and maintain a written, risk-based anti-money-laundering program with a designated compliance officer, internal controls, ongoing training, and independent testing.
sourceNote: Verified via eCFR 31 CFR Part 1025 and FinCEN insurance-company AML/SAR FAQs; applies to life & annuity 'covered products', not P&C-only lines. In force since 2006, current.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN)
title: File Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) for covered insurance products
requirement: An insurance company issuing covered products must report any suspicious transaction conducted or attempted by, at, or through the company that involves at least $5,000 in funds or assets and is known/suspected to involve money laundering, structuring, or other illicit activity. SARs are filed with FinCEN and supporting documentation retained five years.
sourceNote: Verified via eCFR 31 CFR 1025.320 and FinCEN insurance AML/SAR FAQs; $5,000 threshold, 5-year retention. In force, current.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Federal Insurance Office (FIO) / Terrorism Risk Insurance Program
title: Mandatory annual TRIP Data Call submission for commercial P&C insurers
requirement: All insurers writing commercial property/casualty insurance in lines subject to the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program must respond to Treasury's annual TRIP Data Call, registering and submitting terrorism-risk exposure and premium data through the TRIP data portal. For the 2026 call (covering CY2025 data) the deadline is May 15, 2026, and no extensions are granted.
citation: 31 CFR Part 50; 91 FR 14631 (2026 TRIP Data Call)
sourceNote: Verified via Federal Register 2026 TRIP Data Call notice (Mar 25 2026) and Treasury FIO annual-data-collection page; mandatory, due May 15 2026.

regulatorName: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), Benefits Coordination & Recovery Center
title: MMSEA Section 111 mandatory insurer reporting of NGHP settlements/ORM to CMS
requirement: As a Responsible Reporting Entity, a liability, no-fault, or workers' compensation insurer must electronically report to CMS any claim involving a Medicare beneficiary where it assumes Ongoing Responsibility for Medicals (ORM) or makes a Total Payment Obligation to Claimant (TPOC/settlement). Records must be reported within one year of the reporting trigger; late reporting is subject to per-day civil money penalties.
sourceNote: Verified via CMS NGHP Mandatory Insurer Reporting pages and 88 FR final CMP rule; CMP 'compliance clock' began Oct 11 2024, quarterly audits from Jan 2026. Applies across WC/auto/GL liability lines.

title: Report material cybersecurity incidents on Form 8-K Item 1.05 within 4 business days
requirement: An SEC-registered (public) carrier must disclose a material cybersecurity incident on Form 8-K Item 1.05, describing the incident's nature, scope, timing and material impact, within four business days after determining that the incident is material (subject to a limited Attorney-General national-security delay).
sourceNote: Verified via SEC final rule (adopted Jul 26 2023) and SEC compliance guide; Item 1.05 compliance began Dec 18 2023 (Jun 15 2024 for smaller reporting companies). Applies only if SEC-registered.

title: Annual cybersecurity risk-management & governance disclosure in Form 10-K Item 1C
requirement: An SEC-registered carrier must describe, annually in Form 10-K Item 1C (Regulation S-K Item 106), its processes for assessing, identifying and managing material cybersecurity risks, the board's oversight of those risks, and management's role, plus whether cybersecurity threats have materially affected or are reasonably likely to affect the company.
sourceNote: Verified via SEC compliance guide and final rule; Item 106/10-K Item 1C disclosures required for annual reports for fiscal years ending on/after Dec 15 2023. Applies only if SEC-registered.

title: Notify the FTC of a security breach affecting 500+ consumers within 30 days
requirement: A non-bank financial institution subject to FTC jurisdiction (e.g., insurance agencies/finance operations not otherwise supervised) must notify the FTC of a 'notification event' — unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information involving 500 or more consumers — as soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery, via the FTC's online notification form.
sourceNote: Verified via FTC final rule (88 FR, Oct 27 2023) and FTC 'notification requirement now in effect' notice; effective May 13 2024. Scope limited to entities within FTC (not primarily state-insurance-supervised) jurisdiction.

title: Maintain a written information security program under the FTC Safeguards Rule
requirement: A covered non-bank financial institution must develop, implement and maintain a comprehensive written information security program with a qualified individual overseeing it, a written risk assessment, access controls, encryption, MFA, service-provider oversight, an incident response plan, and an annual report to the board or governing body.
sourceNote: Verified via FTC Safeguards Rule text (16 CFR 314); revised program elements fully effective June 9 2023. Scope limited to entities within FTC jurisdiction.

regulatorName: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) / HHS-DOL-Treasury
title: Annual Prescription Drug Data Collection (RxDC) submission to CMS by June 1
requirement: A health insurance issuer of group or individual coverage must annually submit Prescription Drug Data Collection (RxDC) files (plan lists P2/P3 and data files D1-D8 on premiums, enrollment, and top drug/health spending) to CMS through HIOS. The report covering the prior calendar year is due June 1 each year (2025 data due June 1, 2026).
sourceNote: Verified via CMS RxDC program page; annual June 1 deadline, 2025 reference year due June 1 2026. Applies to the carrier's health line.

regulatorName: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) / HHS
title: Publish monthly public machine-readable pricing files (Transparency in Coverage)
requirement: A group or individual health insurance issuer must post and monthly update public machine-readable files disclosing in-network negotiated rates and out-of-network allowed amounts/billed charges for covered items and services, in the CMS-specified schema, on a publicly available website with no access restrictions.
sourceNote: Verified via CMS Health Plan Price Transparency pages and FAQ Part 70; MRF requirement in force since July 1 2022, schema v2.0 phasing in from Feb/Mar 2026. Health line.

regulatorName: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) / HHS
title: Annual Medical Loss Ratio report to HHS and enrollee rebates by September 30
requirement: A health insurance issuer must annually submit its Medical Loss Ratio report to HHS via HIOS and, if its MLR falls below the applicable standard (80% individual/small group, 85% large group), pay premium rebates to enrollees no later than September 30 of the year following the MLR reporting year.
sourceNote: Verified via eCFR 45 CFR Part 158 and CMS MLR resources; annual report + Sept 30 rebate deadline. Health line, in force.

regulatorName: U.S. Departments of HHS, Labor & Treasury
title: No Surprises Act balance-billing protections, QPA and Federal IDR compliance
requirement: A group or individual health plan/issuer must limit patient cost-sharing for out-of-network emergency services and certain non-emergency services at in-network facilities to in-network levels, calculate and disclose the Qualifying Payment Amount, send initial payment or denial within 30 days, and participate in the Federal Independent Dispute Resolution process for disputed provider payments.
sourceNote: Verified via CMS No Surprises Act rules overview; core protections in force since Jan 1 2022, IDR fee final rule effective Jan 22 2024. Health line.

regulatorName: Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), National Flood Insurance Program
title: Sell and service NFIP flood policies under the annual WYO Financial Assistance/Subsidy Arrangement
requirement: A property insurer participating in the NFIP Write Your Own program must execute FEMA's annual Financial Assistance/Subsidy Arrangement and issue, service, adjust, and pay Standard Flood Insurance Policy claims as fiscal agent of the federal government per the WYO Program requirements and NFIP Transaction Record Reporting and Processing (TRRP) standards. The FY arrangement runs Oct 1-Sep 30.
sourceNote: Verified via Federal Register FY2026 (Jan 15 2025) and FY2027 (May 5 2026) WYO Arrangement notices and 44 CFR 62; annual arrangement, FY2027 begins Oct 1 2026. Property line, only if carrier participates in WYO.

regulatorName: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services, Office for Civil Rights (OCR)
title: HIPAA breach notification to individuals, HHS and media for PHI breaches
requirement: A health insurer (HIPAA covered entity) that discovers a breach of unsecured protected health information must notify affected individuals without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery; notify HHS (immediately for breaches of 500+ individuals, annually for smaller breaches by 60 days after year-end); and notify prominent media for breaches affecting 500+ residents of a state/jurisdiction.
sourceNote: Verified via HHS HIPAA breach-notification pages and 45 CFR 164 Subpart D; long-standing, current. Health line (PHI held as covered entity).

regime: Data Protection Act 2018 / DP Charges Regs 2018
title: Annual ICO Data Protection Fee Payment & Registration as Data Controller
requirement: As a data controller processing personal data, the insurer must register with the ICO and pay the annual data protection fee (tier based on size/turnover, up to GBP 2,900) under the Data Protection (Charges and Information) Regulations 2018. The fee must be renewed each year; failure to pay can attract a fixed penalty of up to GBP 4,350.
citation: Data Protection (Charges and Information) Regulations 2018, SI 2018/480
sourceNote: Verified on ico.org.uk data protection fee pages; regime in force since 25 May 2018, fee tiers current as of 2026.

title: 72-Hour Personal Data Breach Notification to the ICO
requirement: On becoming aware of a personal data breach likely to result in a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms, the insurer as controller must notify the ICO without undue delay and, where feasible, no later than 72 hours after becoming aware. Where the risk is high, affected data subjects must also be informed. Failure can attract fines up to GBP 8.7m or 2% of global turnover.
citation: UK GDPR Article 33 & 34; Data Protection Act 2018 Part 3
sourceNote: Verified on ICO personal data breach guidance; UK GDPR Art 33 in force since 1 Jan 2021 (post-Brexit retained EU law), current 2026.

title: Annual Consumer Duty Board Report on Customer Outcomes
requirement: The firm must prepare, at least annually, a report for its governing body setting out the results of its monitoring of consumer outcomes and any actions required. The board must review and approve the assessment, confirm the firm is delivering good outcomes consistent with the Consumer Duty, and agree actions to address any poor outcomes identified.
sourceNote: Verified via FCA Handbook PRIN 2A and FCA good/poor practice publication (Apr 2026); Consumer Duty in force from 31 Jul 2023, board report annual.

title: Ongoing Monitoring & Review of Consumer Outcomes under the Consumer Duty
requirement: The firm must monitor and regularly review the outcomes its retail customers are experiencing across the four outcomes (products/services, price and value, consumer understanding, consumer support), identify where groups of customers are not receiving good outcomes, and take action to address them. This is a continuous obligation feeding the annual board report.
sourceNote: Verified via FCA Handbook PRIN 2A.9 monitoring of consumer outcomes; in force since 31 Jul 2023, current 2026.

title: Annual Fitness & Propriety Certification of Certified Staff (SM&CR)
requirement: Under the Certification Regime, the insurer must assess and certify at least once every 12 months that each employee performing a certification function (who could cause significant harm to the firm or customers) remains fit and proper. Certificates must be issued/renewed annually and appropriate references obtained (looking back 6 years) for relevant hires.
sourceNote: Verified via FCA SM&CR guide for insurers; insurers in SM&CR since Dec 2018. SM&CR reform (PS26/6) underway but annual certification current as of 2026.

title: Senior Manager Approval & Statement of Responsibilities Maintenance (SM&CR)
requirement: Every individual performing a Senior Management Function must be pre-approved by the FCA/PRA, and the firm must maintain and keep up to date a Statement of Responsibilities for each, plus (for larger insurers) a firm Responsibilities Map/Management Responsibilities Map. Changes must be notified and re-approval sought where responsibilities materially change.
sourceNote: Verified via FCA Handbook SUP 10C and SM&CR insurer guide; in force since Dec 2018, current 2026.

title: Operational Resilience: Important Business Services, Impact Tolerances & Self-Assessment
requirement: The firm must identify its important business services, set an impact tolerance for the maximum tolerable disruption to each, carry out mapping and scenario testing to ensure it can remain within tolerance in severe-but-plausible scenarios, and document a board-approved written self-assessment reviewed at least annually. The transitional period to be able to remain within impact tolerances ended 31 March 2025.
sourceNote: Verified via FCA PS21/3; rules effective 31 Mar 2022, full compliance (remain within impact tolerances) required by 31 Mar 2025 - deadline passed, now BAU.

title: PRA Operational Resilience Impact Tolerances for Important Business Services
requirement: As a PRA-authorised insurer, the firm must comply with the PRA Operational Resilience Part rules and SS1/21: identify important business services, set impact tolerances, perform mapping and testing, and maintain a board-approved self-assessment demonstrating it can remain within impact tolerances in severe-but-plausible scenarios. Full compliance was required by 31 March 2025.
citation: PRA Rulebook Operational Resilience Part; PRA SS1/21
sourceNote: Verified via PRA SS1/21 references in FCA/PRA operational resilience materials; effective 31 Mar 2022, transitional end 31 Mar 2025.

title: Annual & Quarterly Solvency UK Regulatory Reporting (UK QRTs)
requirement: The insurer must submit prudential regulatory returns to the PRA under the reformed Solvency UK regime: the consolidated set of UK Quantitative Reporting Templates and National Specific Templates. Under PS15/24, solo firms' quarterly deadlines are 30 business days and annual deadlines 70 business days after the reference date, with a materially reduced (~one third fewer) template set effective 31 December 2024.
citation: PRA Rulebook Reporting Part; PRA PS15/24
sourceNote: Verified via PRA PS15/24 and Solvency UK reporting Q&A (Oct 2025); reformed reporting effective from 31 Dec 2024.

title: Annual Solvency & Financial Condition Report (SFCR) Disclosure
requirement: The insurer must publicly disclose, at least annually, a Solvency and Financial Condition Report covering its business, governance, risk profile, valuation for solvency purposes and capital management, in the structure prescribed by the reformed Solvency UK disclosure rules (PS3/24 reporting and disclosure phase 2), and submit it to the PRA within the applicable deadline.
citation: PRA Rulebook Reporting Part (SFCR); PRA PS3/24
sourceNote: Verified via PRA PS3/24 reporting & disclosure phase 2; SFCR requirement retained under Solvency UK, current 2026.

title: Annual Own Risk and Solvency Assessment (ORSA) Submission to the PRA
requirement: The insurer must conduct and document its Own Risk and Solvency Assessment - a forward-looking self-assessment of its overall solvency needs, continuous compliance with capital requirements and technical provisions, and risk profile - at least annually (and after any significant change in risk profile), and submit the ORSA supervisory report to the PRA.
citation: PRA Rulebook Conditions Governing Business / ORSA
sourceNote: Verified via PRA insurance regulatory reporting pages; ORSA retained under Solvency UK, current 2026.

title: Fair Value Assessment for Manufactured Insurance Products (PROD 4)
requirement: As a manufacturer of non-investment insurance products, the firm's product approval process must identify whether each product provides fair value to customers in the target market and will continue to do so for a reasonably foreseeable period including after renewal, considering total price and all costs. Fair value assessments must be reviewed at appropriate regular intervals and evidenced.
sourceNote: Verified via FCA Handbook PROD 4.2 and FCA thematic review TR24/2 (2024); fair value rules in force since 1 Oct 2021.

title: Manufacturer-to-Distributor Product Value Information Exchange
requirement: As product manufacturer, the firm must provide distributors in the chain with the information they need on the product, its target market and the results of its fair value assessment so distributors can understand and evidence the value the product provides, and must obtain from distributors information (including on their remuneration/distribution costs) needed to assess whether the product continues to offer fair value.
sourceNote: Verified via FCA Handbook PROD 4.2; requirement in force since 1 Oct 2021, reinforced by TR24/2 (2024).

title: Annual Financial Crime Report (REP-CRIM) to the FCA
requirement: In-scope firms (including those carrying on higher money-laundering-risk activities, and firms above the applicable revenue threshold) must submit the annual financial crime data return REP-CRIM to the FCA, covering AML/CTF systems, high-risk customers/jurisdictions, SARs and sanctions exposure, within the deadline after the firm's reporting reference date.
sourceNote: Verified via FCA Handbook SUP 16.23 and FCA PS21/4; extended scope effective 30 Mar 2022, current 2026.

title: Comply with Reformed UK Data Protection Rules under the DUAA 2025
requirement: The insurer must update its UK data protection compliance to reflect the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, which amends the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018 (e.g. recognised legitimate interests, changes to automated decision-making, complaints-handling duties and cookies/PECR). Main Part 5 data-protection changes commence in stages from 2025 into 2026 via commencement regulations.
sourceNote: Verified via GOV.UK DUAA commencement guidance; Royal Assent 19 Jun 2025, phased commencement 2025-2026 (main DP changes ~6 months after assent).

title: Provision of IPID and Pre-Contract Product Information to Insurance Customers
requirement: Before conclusion of a non-investment insurance contract, the firm must give the customer appropriate, objective and relevant information about the policy in good time and in a comprehensible form (including a standardised Insurance Product Information Document for general insurance) so the customer can make an informed decision, consistent with Consumer Duty communication rules.
sourceNote: Verified via FCA Handbook ICOBS 6.1; IPID requirement in force since IDD implementation (1 Oct 2018), current 2026.

regulatorName: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) / national competent authority
title: DORA ICT Risk Management Framework establishment & board oversight
requirement: Insurance/reinsurance undertakings must establish, maintain and document a sound, comprehensive ICT risk-management framework with board-level accountability, covering identification, protection, detection, response, recovery and learning. The management body approves and reviews the framework. Applicable from 17 January 2025.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex and EIOPA DORA page; DORA entered into application 17 Jan 2025.

regulatorName: National competent authority (e.g. BaFin, ACPR) coordinating with EIOPA
title: DORA major ICT-related incident reporting (initial/intermediate/final) to NCA
requirement: Undertakings must classify ICT-related incidents and report major incidents to their national competent authority via a staged cascade: an initial notification, an intermediate report, and a final report, on the deadlines set by the RTS/ITS. Significant cyber threats may be voluntarily notified. Applicable from 17 January 2025.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 19 and EIOPA DORA page; reporting templates in Commission Implementing/Delegated Regs supplementing DORA.

regulatorName: National competent authority coordinating with EIOPA
title: DORA Register of Information on ICT third-party arrangements — annual submission
requirement: Undertakings must maintain, at entity/sub-consolidated/consolidated level, a Register of Information on all contractual arrangements for ICT services from third-party providers, and report it at least yearly to the competent authority in the machine-readable format prescribed by the ITS. Applicable from 17 January 2025; first submissions ran in 2025.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; ITS (EU) 2024/2956 defines 15 templates, xBRL-CSV, annual reference date 31 Dec.

regulatorName: National competent authority coordinating with EIOPA
title: DORA digital operational resilience testing programme (annual basic testing)
requirement: Undertakings must establish a risk-based digital operational resilience testing programme and perform appropriate tests on ICT tools and systems supporting critical/important functions at least annually (vulnerability assessments, scans, gap analyses, penetration tests, etc.). Applicable from 17 January 2025.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex and EIOPA DORA page.

regulatorName: National competent authority coordinating with EIOPA
title: DORA Threat-Led Penetration Testing (TLPT) for significant entities
requirement: Undertakings identified by the competent authority as significant must conduct advanced Threat-Led Penetration Testing on live production systems supporting critical/important functions at least every three years, engaging qualified testers and including relevant ICT third parties. Applicable from 17 January 2025.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; TLPT at least every 3 years for entities designated by NCA.

regulatorName: National competent authority coordinating with EIOPA
title: DORA ICT third-party contractual & concentration-risk requirements
requirement: Undertakings must adopt an ICT third-party risk strategy, assess concentration risk, and ensure contracts for ICT services supporting critical/important functions contain the mandatory clauses (access/audit rights, exit strategies, service levels, sub-outsourcing, data location). Applicable from 17 January 2025.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; key contractual provisions in Art. 30.

regulatorName: National market surveillance authority (AI Act) / EIOPA guidance
title: EU AI Act high-risk compliance for life/health insurance risk-assessment & pricing AI
requirement: AI systems used for risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance are high-risk under Annex III(5)(c). Providers must meet the high-risk requirements (risk management, data governance, technical documentation, logging, transparency, human oversight, accuracy/robustness). The AI Act entered into force 1 Aug 2024; high-risk (Annex III) obligations apply from 2 Aug 2026 (a proposed Digital Omnibus deferral to Dec 2027 is not yet adopted).
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex and artificialintelligenceact.eu; high-risk application date 2 Aug 2026 as enacted (omnibus deferral pending as of July 2026).

title: EU AI Act Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (FRIA) for insurance-pricing AI deployers
requirement: As a deployer of a high-risk AI system for risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance, the carrier must, before first use, perform a fundamental rights impact assessment (use description, affected persons, risks, human-oversight and remediation measures) and notify the results to the market surveillance authority. Applies with the high-risk regime from 2 Aug 2026.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 27 and AI Act Service Desk; FRIA duty extends to life/health insurance risk-assessment & pricing deployers.

regulatorName: European Commission / national market surveillance authority
title: EU AI Act registration of high-risk AI system in the EU database
requirement: Before placing on the market or putting into service a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III (incl. insurance pricing/risk-assessment), the provider (and deployers that are public bodies) must register the system and required information in the EU database maintained by the Commission. Applies with the high-risk regime from 2 Aug 2026.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 49 and AI Act Service Desk; EU database registration for Annex III systems.

title: EU AI Act AI-literacy obligation for staff operating AI systems
requirement: Providers and deployers of AI systems must ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy among staff and others operating AI on their behalf, taking account of their technical knowledge, experience and the context of use. This general obligation has applied since 2 February 2025.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; Art. 4 AI-literacy duty applicable from 2 Feb 2025 (Art. 113).

regulatorName: National competent authority (supervisor) under Solvency II
title: Solvency II annual Solvency & Financial Condition Report (SFCR) public disclosure
requirement: Insurance and reinsurance undertakings must publicly disclose, at least annually, a Solvency and Financial Condition Report (SFCR) covering business & performance, system of governance, risk profile, valuation for solvency purposes and capital management, with prescribed quantitative templates annexed. Directive (EU) 2025/2 restructures the SFCR into policyholder and professional parts, applicable at the latest from 30 January 2027.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex and EIOPA; amending Directive (EU) 2025/2 published 8 Jan 2025, applies at latest 30 Jan 2027.

regulatorName: National competent authority (supervisor) under Solvency II
title: Solvency II Regular Supervisory Report & Quantitative Reporting Templates (QRTs)
requirement: Undertakings must submit to the supervisor the Regular Supervisory Report (RSR) and the periodic Quantitative Reporting Templates (annual and quarterly) prescribed by the reporting ITS. Directive (EU) 2025/2 extends deadlines (annual QRTs 14→16 weeks; RSR/SFCR 14→18 weeks) applying from year-end 2027.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex/EIOPA; reporting ITS 2023/894, revised deadlines & Taxonomy 2.x apply from YE2027 per Directive (EU) 2025/2.

regulatorName: National competent authority (supervisor) under Solvency II
title: Solvency II Own Risk and Solvency Assessment (ORSA) & supervisory report
requirement: As part of its risk-management system, every undertaking must conduct, at least annually and after any significant change in its risk profile, an Own Risk and Solvency Assessment (ORSA) of overall solvency needs, continuous compliance with capital requirements and technical provisions, and report the results to the supervisory authority.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex Art. 45 and EIOPA ORSA guidelines; results reported to supervisor under Art. 35 Pillar 3.

regulatorName: National competent authority (supervisor) under Solvency II
title: Solvency II Solvency Capital Requirement (SCR) & Minimum Capital Requirement (MCR) coverage
requirement: Undertakings must at all times hold eligible own funds covering the Solvency Capital Requirement (calculated by the standard formula or an approved internal model) and the Minimum Capital Requirement, and immediately notify the supervisor and submit a recovery/finance scheme upon any breach.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; SCR/MCR coverage and breach-notification duties in Pillar 1.

title: IDD Product Oversight & Governance (POG) — product approval process for manufacturers
requirement: As a manufacturer of insurance products, the carrier must maintain, operate and review a product approval process specifying an identified target market, assessing all relevant risks and consistency with that target market, and a distribution strategy, plus regular product review. Applies to each product manufactured for sale to customers.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex and EIOPA rulebook; POG detailed by Delegated Reg (EU) 2017/2358, in force.

title: IDD Insurance Product Information Document (IPID) for non-life products
requirement: The manufacturer of a non-life insurance product must draw up a standardised Insurance Product Information Document (IPID) in the prescribed format, provided to the customer before conclusion of the contract, covering type of insurance, main risks insured, sum insured, exclusions, obligations and how/when to pay.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex/EIOPA and LexisNexis; IPID format set by Implementing Reg (EU) 2017/1469.

title: IDD demands-and-needs test before every insurance contract
requirement: Before the conclusion of any insurance contract, the distributor must specify, on the basis of information obtained from the customer, the customer's demands and needs, and ensure any contract proposed is consistent with them; where advice is given, a personalised recommendation must be provided.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex and EIOPA Q&A; demands-and-needs test mandatory for all products.

title: IDD suitability/appropriateness assessment for insurance-based investment products (IBIPs)
requirement: When distributing insurance-based investment products, the undertaking/intermediary must obtain the necessary information on the customer's knowledge, experience, financial situation (ability to bear losses) and objectives (risk tolerance) to assess suitability (advised sales) or appropriateness (non-advised), and provide a periodic suitability report.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex/EIOPA; IBIP conduct rules detailed by Delegated Reg (EU) 2017/2359.

regulatorName: Competent supervisory authority under the PRIIPs Regulation
title: PRIIPs Key Information Document (KID) for insurance-based investment products
requirement: The manufacturer of an insurance-based investment product (a PRIIP) must draw up and publish a standardised, up-to-date Key Information Document (KID) — including risk indicator, performance scenarios and costs — and the distributor must provide it to retail investors in good time before conclusion of the contract.
citation: Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014, Arts. 5, 8, 13; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/653
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; PRIIPs KID mandatory for IBIPs, RTS in Delegated Reg (EU) 2017/653 (as amended).

regulatorName: National competent authority under the SFDR
title: SFDR sustainability-related disclosures for insurance-based investment products
requirement: As a financial market participant offering insurance-based investment products, the carrier must publish website, pre-contractual and periodic disclosures on the integration of sustainability risks, principal adverse impacts, and, for Article 8/9 products, environmental/social characteristics or sustainable-investment objectives.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; SFDR applies to IBIP manufacturers; RTS in Delegated Reg (EU) 2022/1288, applicable since Jan 2023.

title: CSRD sustainability reporting under the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS)
requirement: Large EU insurance undertakings in scope must include, in the management report, sustainability information prepared to the ESRS (double-materiality, climate, own workforce, governance) with limited assurance. Note: the 2025 'Stop-the-clock' Directive (EU) 2025/794 postponed reporting waves and a substantive Omnibus revision is pending; verify the entity's applicable first-reporting year.
citation: Directive 2013/34/EU as amended by Directive (EU) 2022/2464; Directive (EU) 2025/794
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; CSRD/ESRS scope for large undertakings, timelines deferred by 'Stop-the-clock' Directive (EU) 2025/794 (2025); Omnibus still in negotiation as of July 2026.

regulatorName: National competent authority under AMLD / national FIU
title: EU AML/CFT customer due diligence & suspicious-transaction reporting for life insurance
requirement: As an obliged entity carrying on life-assurance and other investment-related insurance, the carrier must apply customer due diligence, identify beneficial owners and beneficiaries, and report suspicious transactions to the national Financial Intelligence Unit. The single AML Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 and AMLD6 (EU) 2024/1640 apply mainly from 10 July 2027.
sourceNote: Verified on EUR-Lex; life insurers are obliged entities; new AML package (Reg 2024/1624 / AMLD6) largely applies 10 July 2027, current AMLD in force until then.

regulatorName: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
title: PIPEDA Breach of Security Safeguards Report to OPC & Affected Individuals
requirement: Report to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner and notify affected individuals (and relevant third parties) of any breach of security safeguards involving personal information that creates a real risk of significant harm, as soon as feasible after determining a breach occurred. Pass condition: OPC report filed and individual notifications issued for every qualifying breach.
sourceNote: Verified on OPC (priv.gc.ca); mandatory breach reporting in force since Nov 1, 2018 under PIPEDA and the Breach of Security Safeguards Regulations; current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
title: PIPEDA Breach Records Register — Maintain 24-Month Log of All Breaches
requirement: Maintain a record of every breach of security safeguards involving personal information under the organization's control, whether or not it meets the real-risk-of-significant-harm threshold, in sufficient detail for the OPC to verify compliance. Records must be kept for 24 months and produced to the OPC on request.
sourceNote: Verified on OPC guidance gd_pb_201810; 24-month retention requirement in force since Nov 1, 2018; current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec
title: Quebec Law 25 Confidentiality Incident Notification to CAI & Individuals
requirement: Where a confidentiality incident involving personal information presents a risk of serious injury, promptly notify the Commission d'accès à l'information (CAI) and each affected individual, take reasonable measures to reduce the risk, and record the incident in a confidentiality incident register. Pass condition: CAI and individual notifications made without delay for every qualifying incident.
citation: Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, CQLR c. P-39.1, s. 3.5
sourceNote: Verified on LegisQuebec; s. 3.5 incident-notification provisions in force since Sept 22, 2022 under Law 25 (Bill 64); current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec
title: Quebec Law 25 Designation of Privacy Officer & Published Governance Policies
requirement: Designate a person responsible for the protection of personal information (privacy officer; the highest-authority person by default unless delegated in writing) and establish, implement and publish governance policies and practices for the personal information held. Pass condition: officer designated and title/contact plus governance rules published on the enterprise website.
citation: Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, CQLR c. P-39.1, ss. 3.1–3.2
sourceNote: Verified on LegisQuebec; privacy-officer and governance-policy duties in force since Sept 22, 2022 under Law 25; current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec
title: Quebec Law 25 Privacy Impact Assessment for Systems & Cross-Border Transfers
requirement: Conduct a privacy impact assessment for any project to acquire, develop or overhaul an information system or electronic service delivery involving personal information, and before communicating personal information outside Quebec, assessing the adequacy of protection. Pass condition: a documented PIA is completed before each qualifying project or transfer.
citation: Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, CQLR c. P-39.1, ss. 3.3 & 17
sourceNote: Verified on LegisQuebec; PIA obligations in force since Sept 22, 2023 (systems) with cross-border transfer PIA under s.17; current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec
title: Quebec Law 25 Data Portability — Provide Computerized Personal Information on Request
requirement: On request by an individual, provide the computerized personal information collected from them in a structured, commonly used technological format, or transfer it to a designated third party. Pass condition: portable-format data provided/transferred within the statutory timeframe for each valid request.
citation: Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, CQLR c. P-39.1, s. 27
sourceNote: Verified on LegisQuebec; the data-portability right became effective Sept 22, 2024 — the final phase of Law 25; current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
title: OSFI B-13 Technology & Cyber Risk Management Program for Federally Regulated Insurers
requirement: Federally regulated insurers must establish and maintain a technology and cyber risk management program across the three domains of governance & risk management, technology operations & resilience, and cyber security, proportionate to their size and risk profile. Pass condition: a board/senior-management-overseen program meeting B-13's expectations is in place and maintained.
citation: OSFI Guideline B-13 (Technology and Cyber Risk Management)
sourceNote: Verified on osfi-bsif.gc.ca; Guideline B-13 effective Jan 1, 2024 for FRFIs including insurers; current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
title: OSFI Technology & Cyber Security Incident Report Within 24 Hours
requirement: Report any technology or cyber security incident that has, or could have, an impact on operations or the confidentiality, integrity or availability of systems and information to OSFI in writing within 24 hours (or sooner if possible), with follow-up updates through resolution. Pass condition: initial notification to OSFI submitted within 24 hours of each qualifying incident.
citation: OSFI Advisory: Technology and Cyber Security Incident Reporting (Aug 2021)
sourceNote: Verified on osfi-bsif.gc.ca; the 24-hour reporting Advisory took effect Aug 13, 2021, tightening the prior 72-hour rule; current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
title: OSFI Integrity & Security Program (incl. Background Checks) for FRFIs
requirement: Federally regulated insurers must maintain policies and procedures protecting integrity and security against threats including foreign interference and undue influence, covering governance, people (including background checks), technology, data and physical security. Pass condition: an integrity-and-security program meeting the ten guideline expectations is implemented and maintained.
sourceNote: Verified on osfi-bsif.gc.ca; compliance required by Jan 31, 2025 (general) and July 31, 2025 (background checks); current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
title: OSFI E-21 Operational Resilience — Critical Operations Mapping & Impact Tolerances
requirement: Federally regulated insurers must identify critical operations, set tolerances for disruption, map internal/third-party/ICT dependencies, and operationalize an operational risk and resilience framework, with scenario testing of critical operations. Pass condition: full adherence to E-21's resilience expectations by the Sept 1, 2026 phase and scenario testing completed by Sept 1, 2027.
citation: OSFI Guideline E-21 (Operational Risk Management and Resilience)
sourceNote: Verified on osfi-bsif.gc.ca; E-21 published Aug 22, 2024 with phased dates Sept 1 2025/2026/2027; current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
title: OSFI B-10 Enterprise-Wide Third-Party Risk Management Framework
requirement: Federally regulated insurers must maintain an enterprise-wide third-party risk management framework governing business and strategic arrangements with third parties, applying proportionate controls (contract provisions, security, monitoring) based on criticality and risk, and updating legacy arrangements at renewal. Pass condition: a compliant TPRM framework is in place and applied to all in-scope arrangements.
sourceNote: Verified on osfi-bsif.gc.ca; revised B-10 effective May 1, 2024 for FRFIs (excludes foreign branches); current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
title: OSFI B-15 Annual Climate-Related Financial Disclosure (IFRS S2-aligned)
requirement: Federally regulated insurers must publish annual climate-related financial disclosures aligned with Annex 2-2 (IFRS S2) across governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics & targets pillars, no later than 180 days after fiscal year-end. Pass condition: compliant disclosure published annually within the 180-day window.
sourceNote: Verified on osfi-bsif.gc.ca; disclosure effective FY2024 for IAIGs/D-SIBs and FY2025 for other in-scope FRFIs; updated guideline Mar 7, 2025; current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
title: FINTRAC AML/ATF Compliance Program for Life Insurers
requirement: Life insurance companies, brokers and agents must implement and maintain a compliance program including an appointed compliance officer, written policies and procedures, a risk assessment, ongoing training, and a biennial effectiveness review. Pass condition: all five compliance-program elements are documented, current, and reviewed at least every two years.
citation: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, s. 9.6
sourceNote: Verified on FINTRAC (canada.ca); compliance-program obligation under PCMLTFA in force and current; guidance current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
title: FINTRAC Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR) for Life Insurers
requirement: Life insurance companies, brokers and agents must submit a Suspicious Transaction Report to FINTRAC as soon as practicable after taking measures that establish reasonable grounds to suspect a transaction (or attempted transaction) is related to money laundering or terrorist financing. Pass condition: an STR is filed for every qualifying suspicion.
citation: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, s. 7
sourceNote: Verified on FINTRAC (canada.ca); STR obligation in force under PCMLTFA s.7; life-insurer guidance current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
title: FINTRAC Large Cash & Large Virtual Currency Transaction Reports (24-Hour Rule)
requirement: Life insurance companies, brokers and agents must file Large Cash Transaction Reports and Large Virtual Currency Transaction Reports with FINTRAC for receipts of CAD 10,000 or more (including within the 24-hour aggregation rule) within the prescribed timeframe. Pass condition: an LCTR/LVCTR is submitted for every reportable transaction.
citation: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, ss. 9 & 12.1
sourceNote: Verified on FINTRAC (canada.ca); LVCTR guidance updated May 17, 2024; LCTR/LVCTR 24-hour rule current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
title: FINTRAC Beneficial Ownership Collection & Confirmation for Life Insurers
