requirement: Life insurance companies, brokers and agents must obtain beneficial ownership information for entity clients and take reasonable measures to confirm its accuracy, keeping records up to date, with discrepancy-related expectations effective October 2025. Pass condition: beneficial ownership is collected, confirmed, and recorded for every entity client.
sourceNote: Verified on FINTRAC beneficial-ownership guidance (canada.ca); requirement in force with discrepancy expectations from Oct 2025; current as of 2026.

title: BMA Annual Statutory Financial Return for Commercial (Re)insurers
requirement: A commercial (re)insurer registered in Bermuda must prepare and file its annual statutory financial return (including statutory financial statements and Bermuda Solvency Capital Requirement schedules) with the Bermuda Monetary Authority for each financial year within the prescribed deadline. Pass condition: complete statutory financial return filed on time for the financial year.
citation: Insurance Act 1978, s. 17 & s. 18 (statutory financial return)
sourceNote: Verified on bma.bm; annual statutory financial return / BSCR filing under the Insurance Act 1978 for commercial classes; current as of 2026 filing cycle.

title: BMA BSCR / Enhanced Capital Requirement Annual Filing (120% Target Capital)
requirement: A commercial (re)insurer must calculate and file its Enhanced Capital Requirement using the applicable Bermuda Solvency Capital Requirement (BSCR) model or an approved internal capital model, maintaining eligible capital at or above the ECR and a Target Capital Level of at least 120% of ECR. Pass condition: BSCR/ECR schedules filed annually and capital held at/above the required levels.
citation: Insurance (Prudential Standards) (Class 4 and Class 3B Solvency Requirement) Rules 2008
sourceNote: Verified on bma.bm; BSCR/ECR calibrated to 99% TVaR one-year with 120% TCL; current for the 2026 filing cycle.

title: BMA Commercial Insurer's Solvency Self-Assessment (CISSA) Annual Filing
requirement: A commercial (re)insurer must conduct and file its Commercial Insurer's Solvency Self-Assessment (CISSA) with the BMA annually, documenting its own assessment of the capital required to support current and prospective risks over its business planning horizon. Pass condition: a board-approved CISSA is filed for the financial year.
citation: Insurance (Prudential Standards) (Class 4 and Class 3B Solvency Requirement) Rules 2008 (CISSA)
sourceNote: Verified on bma.bm; CISSA is the Bermuda ORSA-equivalent required annually of commercial insurers; current as of 2026.

title: BMA Financial Condition Report (FCR) Filing & Website Publication
requirement: A commercial (re)insurer must file a Financial Condition Report signed by its chief executive and senior function heads (actuarial, risk, internal audit or compliance) with the BMA, and publish the FCR on the insurer's website within 14 days of filing. Pass condition: FCR filed annually and posted publicly within 14 days.
citation: Insurance Act 1978, s. 6A / Insurance (Public Disclosure) Rules 2015 (FCR)
sourceNote: Verified on bma.bm public-filing guidelines; FCR must be published on the insurer's website within 14 days of filing; current as of 2026.

title: BMA Audited GAAP Financial Statements Filing for Commercial (Re)insurers
requirement: A commercial (re)insurer (Class 4/3B/3A, C/D/E and Groups) must file audited general purpose financial statements prepared under an acceptable GAAP (Bermuda, Canada, UK or US) with the BMA within four months of financial year-end (extendable up to seven months on application). Pass condition: audited financial statements filed within the applicable deadline.
citation: Insurance Act 1978, s. 17A (audited GAAP / general purpose financial statements)
sourceNote: Verified on bma.bm; four-month (up to seven with approval) filing window; GAAP of Bermuda/Canada/UK/US accepted; current as of 2026.

title: BMA Annual Declaration of Compliance for Commercial (Re)insurers
requirement: A commercial (re)insurer (Class 4/3B/3A, C/D/E) must file an annual Declaration of Compliance with the BMA confirming it met the minimum criteria for registration and applicable prudential requirements throughout the financial year. Pass condition: signed Declaration of Compliance filed as part of the annual filing.
sourceNote: Verified on bma.bm year-end filing requirements for Class 4/3B and other commercial classes; current as of 2026 filing cycle.

title: ECDIS & predictive-model governance & risk management framework (Reg 10-1-1) with annual attestation
requirement: Insurers using external consumer data and information sources (ECDIS) or ECDIS-based algorithms/predictive models must establish and document a cross-functional governance and risk management framework to prevent unfair discrimination, and file a compliance progress report then an annual attestation of full compliance with the Division. Originally life-only; the amended regulation (effective Oct 15, 2025) extends it to individual life, private passenger auto and health benefit plan insurers. Pass condition: a documented GRM framework plus timely attestation.
sourceNote: Original effective Nov 14, 2023; amended reg (adds auto & health) effective Oct 15, 2025; verified via Colorado DORA adoption notices.

title: Quantitative testing of ECDIS & predictive models for unfair discrimination (life insurers) with annual report
requirement: Life insurers that use ECDIS, algorithms or predictive models must conduct quantitative testing to detect unfair discrimination against protected classes and submit an annual report describing the testing methodology, assumptions, results and remediation, per Bulletin B-10.004 implementing the SB 21-169 framework. First reports due Dec 1, 2024 and annually thereafter. Pass condition: documented quantitative testing plus timely annual report to the Division.
citation: Colorado Bulletin B-10.004 (Quantitative Testing Reporting Requirement for Life Insurers using ECDIS), under 3 CCR 702-10
sourceNote: Bulletin B-10.004 adopted Oct 18, 2024; annual quantitative-testing reports due Dec 1 each year; verified via Colorado DORA adoption notice.

regulatorName: New York State Department of Financial Services
title: AI/ECDIS governance, fairness testing & consumer disclosure for underwriting and pricing (NY)
requirement: Insurers authorized in New York using AI systems (AIS) or external consumer data and information sources (ECDIS) in underwriting or pricing must maintain a board/senior-management-overseen governance framework, demonstrate the data/model is not based on and does not produce unlawful/proxy discrimination under Insurance Law Article 26 (including a proxy/quantitative fairness analysis), and provide consumer transparency. Applies to all lines. Pass condition: documented governance plus a passing unfair-discrimination/proxy analysis before and during AIS/ECDIS use.
sourceNote: Final circular issued Jul 11, 2024; articulates how existing NY Insurance Law applies to AIS/ECDIS; verified on dfs.ny.gov.

title: Anti-discrimination controls & records for AI/Big Data in marketing, rating, underwriting & claims (CA)
requirement: Insurers must avoid unfair discrimination and proxy discrimination when using AI, algorithms or Big Data in marketing, rating, underwriting, claims and fraud investigation affecting California residents, and must be able to demonstrate/document that models and data sources do not produce prohibited discriminatory outcomes. Applies to all lines. Pass condition: controls and documentation showing AI/Big Data use complies with the Insurance Code and Fair Claims/anti-discrimination law.
sourceNote: Issued Jun 30, 2022; still in force; verified on insurance.ca.gov. (CA has not adopted the NAIC AI Model Bulletin; this is its standing AI/Big Data guidance.)

title: Biennial Wildfire Risk Information Report for admitted residential property insurers
requirement: Admitted insurers with $10M or more of California residential property direct written premium must file a biennial wildfire risk information report to the CA DOI covering the prior two years of residential experience — per-policy fire/wildfire-incurred losses by coverage category, protection class, fire risk score, premium and ZIP code. Required under Insurance Code section 929 as amended by SB 824.
sourceNote: Verified on CA DOI Wildfire Risk Info Reporting page July 2026; biennial, $10M threshold

title: Catastrophe Reporting Form claims submission via IRFS after each activated event
requirement: When OIR activates a catastrophe data call following a hurricane or other catastrophic event, all authorized insurers must file county and statewide claims data on the current-year Catastrophe Reporting Form via the Insurance Regulation Filing System (IRFS) at OIR-set intervals. Covers homeowners, dwelling, mobile homeowners, commercial residential/property, private flood and business interruption. Insurers with no in-force policies or claims must still make a 'No Data' filing.
sourceNote: Verified on FLOIR Catastrophe Reporting page July 2026; 2026 form CRF-26A; event-activated

title: Annual TWIA catastrophe-area property premium data call with affidavit
requirement: TDI conducts an annual data call requiring specified insurers writing property/commercial lines in the Texas catastrophe area to report prior-year Texas property direct written premium used to calculate TWIA assessment participation shares. Respondents must submit the TWIA Data Call Form plus a separately emailed affidavit, even if they write no applicable business. Authorized by Insurance Code § 2210.052.
sourceNote: Verified on TDI Bulletin B-0002-26 July 2026; 2025 data due May 22, 2026

title: Catastrophe event claims reporting under the TX Catastrophe Event Statistical Plan
requirement: When TDI activates its catastrophe data call for a specified event, insurers writing personal and commercial property risks must report claims and loss data under the Texas Catastrophe Event Statistical Plan at the frequency and due dates TDI announces by bulletin. Reporting is not required until TDI activates the call for a named event.
citation: Texas Catastrophe Event Statistical Plan for Personal and Commercial Risks (28 TAC)
sourceNote: Verified on TDI Catastrophe Event Statistical Plan July 2026; event-activated reporting

regulatorName: NAIC / U.S. Treasury Federal Insurance Office
regime: NAIC Property & Casualty Market Intelligence (PCMI) Data Call
title: NAIC Homeowners Market Intelligence (PCMI) climate-peril data call submission
requirement: Under the NAIC-coordinated Property & Casualty Market Intelligence data call, homeowners insurers writing at least $50,000 in relevant homeowners premium must submit ZIP-code-level data on premiums, claims/losses by peril, deductibles, cancellations, non-renewals, coverage limits and mitigation discounts. The 2026 call covers policy years 2018-2025 with data due June 15, 2026.
citation: NAIC Property & Casualty Market Intelligence Data Call (2026 Homeowners)
sourceNote: Verified on NAIC data call page and NAIC article July 2026; 2026 call, $50k threshold, due June 15, 2026

title: California FAIR Plan mandatory membership, participation & premium reporting
requirement: Every insurer licensed to write basic property insurance in California must be a member of the California FAIR Plan Association and share its writings, expenses, profits and losses in proportion to its premiums written during the second preceding calendar year (excluding FAIR Plan premium). Members must report premium data annually so participation rates can be set. Pass condition: current membership and timely reporting of premium data.
sourceNote: Verified via CA Ins. Code 10090 et seq. (FAIR Plan, enacted 1968) and CDI; participation per 10095(c). Current as of 2026.

title: California FAIR Plan wildfire assessment payment by member insurers (2025 framework)
requirement: Upon a Commissioner-approved FAIR Plan assessment, each member insurer must pay its allocated share (personal/commercial lines, based on prior premium participation rate) within the stated deadline. The Feb 2025 Order 2025-1 approved up to $1B personal + $1B commercial for the Jan 2025 LA/Ventura wildfires; recoupment of paid amounts follows Bulletin 2025-4. Pass condition: full and timely assessment payment.
citation: Cal. Ins. Code section 10094; CDI Order No. 2025-1; Bulletin 2025-4
sourceNote: Verified via CDI Order 2025-1 (executed Feb 11, 2025) approving up to $2B assessment; Bulletin 2025-4 recoupment guidance. Current as of 2026.

title: Florida Citizens mandatory membership, assessment participation & premium reporting
requirement: All insurers authorized to write property (or property/casualty) insurance in Florida are members of Citizens and must pay regular, emergency, and Citizens Policyholder Surcharge assessments on the statutory formula, and must collect and remit emergency assessments from their own policyholders. Members report statewide direct written premium so shares can be computed. Pass condition: timely assessment remittance and premium reporting.
sourceNote: Verified via Fla. Stat. 627.351(6) (Citizens); emergency-assessment collect/remit duty and 10%/premium caps. Current 2024 statute text as of 2026.

title: Texas FAIR Plan mandatory membership, deficit assessment & premium reporting
requirement: Each insurer writing residential property insurance in Texas must be a member of the Texas FAIR Plan Association and participate in its writings, expenses, assessments, profits and losses in proportion to its net direct residential property premiums. Members pay deficit assessments within 30 days of notice (non-payment triggers COA suspension) and report premium for participation. Pass condition: membership and timely assessment payment.
sourceNote: Verified via Tex. Ins. Code Ch. 2211 and TDI; Dec 2024 ($17.6M) and Sept 2025 ($60.1M) member assessments confirm active. Current as of 2026.

title: Texas Windstorm Association (TWIA) mandatory membership & catastrophe loss assessment
requirement: All insurers licensed to write property insurance in Texas must be members of the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association; following a catastrophe in the coastal territory that exhausts premium and other funding layers, member insurers share Association losses via Class 2/3 member assessments based on their statutory participation percentage. Members report premium for participation. Pass condition: membership and timely member assessment payment.
sourceNote: Verified via Tex. Ins. Code Ch. 2210 and TDI TWIA overview; post-2009 funding stack with member assessments. Current as of 2026.

title: Louisiana Citizens mandatory participation, regular assessment collect & remit
requirement: All insurers authorized and writing property insurance in Louisiana must participate in the Coastal Plan and FAIR Plan operated by LA Citizens as a condition of authority. On a plan-year deficit, LA Citizens may levy a regular assessment up to 10% of industry premium on assessable lines; insurers must remit and may recoup from policyholders. Pass condition: participation and timely assessment remittance.
sourceNote: Verified via La. R.S. 22:2293 (creation of LA Citizens) and LDI/LA Citizens assessment guidelines; 10% regular-assessment cap. Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: New York State Department of Financial Services
title: NYPIUA (NY FAIR Plan) mandatory membership, participation & premium reporting
requirement: Every insurer authorized to write fire, extended coverage and homeowners insurance in New York on a direct basis must be a member of the NY Property Insurance Underwriting Association as a condition of authority, and participates in its writings, expenses, profits and losses in proportion to its net direct premiums. Members are subject to assessment and report premium. Pass condition: membership and timely assessment/premium reporting.
sourceNote: Verified via N.Y. Ins. Law Art. 54 (sections 5401-5412) and NYPIUA; membership condition of authority. Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
title: NJ Insurance Underwriting Association (FAIR Plan) mandatory participation & surcharge
requirement: Every insurer authorized to write property insurance in New Jersey must participate in the NJ Insurance Underwriting Association (FAIR Plan). Members share writings/losses on premium volume; the Commissioner establishes a surcharge (capped at 5% of statewide basic-property premium) on basic property policies, and members report premium. Pass condition: participation and correct surcharge collection/remittance.
sourceNote: Verified via N.J.S.A. 17:37A-19 (mandatory participation) and 17:37A-20 (5% surcharge cap); NJ DOBI. Current as of 2026.

regime: MA Property Insurance Underwriting Association (FAIR Plan)
title: MPIUA (MA FAIR Plan) mandatory membership, loss-sharing & premium reporting
requirement: All insurers licensed to write basic property insurance in Massachusetts must be members of the MA Property Insurance Underwriting Association (FAIR Plan) as a condition of authority, sharing losses on a premium-volume basis (with adjusted participation ratios for credit-eligible zip codes). Members report premium and are subject to assessment. Pass condition: membership and timely premium reporting/loss sharing.
sourceNote: Verified via M.G.L. c. 175C (joint underwriting association) and MPIUA/Mass.gov; membership condition of authority. Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Georgia Office of Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire
title: Georgia Underwriting Association (FAIR Plan) mandatory participation & assessment
requirement: All insurers licensed to write and writing property insurance in Georgia on a direct basis must participate in the FAIR Plan / Georgia Underwriting Association and share on a fair and equitable basis all expenses, income and losses. Members report premium to determine participation and are subject to assessment. Pass condition: participation and timely assessment/premium reporting.
sourceNote: Verified via O.C.G.A. 33-33-1 (establishment) and 33-33-3 (required participation); GA OCI. Current 2024 code as of 2026.

title: Ohio FAIR Plan mandatory membership, participation & assessment
requirement: Insurers writing basic property insurance in Ohio are members of the Ohio FAIR Plan Underwriting Association and participate in its writings, expenses, profits and losses in proportion to premiums written vs. aggregate member premiums; the plan of operation provides for assessment of members sufficient to operate the association (with reallocation for insolvent members). Pass condition: membership and timely assessment payment.
sourceNote: Verified via ORC 3929.43 and Ohio Admin. Code 3901-1-18 (plan of operation); Ohio DOI. Current as of 2026.

title: Illinois FAIR Plan mandatory membership, apportionment & assessment
requirement: All insurers writing basic property insurance (or property components of multi-peril policies) in Illinois must belong to the Industry Placement Facility administering the FAIR Plan and share equitable apportionment; the program may assess members in amounts sufficient to operate the facility, recovered via a uniform premium percentage over three years. Members report premium. Pass condition: membership and timely assessment.
sourceNote: Verified via 215 ILCS 5/ Art. XXXIII (Urban Property Insurance / FAIR Plan) and Illinois FAIR Plan Association. Current 2024 code as of 2026.

title: NC Insurance Underwriting Association (Coastal/Beach Plan) mandatory membership
requirement: Every insurer authorized to write essential property insurance in North Carolina must be a member of the NC Insurance Underwriting Association (Coastal Property Insurance Pool / Beach Plan) as a condition of authority, sharing profits and losses per its participation, subject to assessment, with annual credits for property voluntarily written in the beach/coastal areas. Members report premium. Pass condition: membership and timely reporting/assessment.
sourceNote: Verified via N.C.G.S. Ch. 58 Art. 45 (sections 58-45-5, 58-45-10); membership condition of authority. Current 2025 code as of 2026.

regime: SC Wind and Hail Underwriting Association
title: SC Wind & Hail Association mandatory membership, annual premium call & participation
requirement: All private insurers authorized to write property insurance in South Carolina on a direct, statewide basis are members of the SC Wind and Hail Underwriting Association (coastal residual market). Members must respond to the Annual Call for Premium so participation rates can be set, share profits/losses per participation, and may reduce participation via voluntary coastal wind writings. Pass condition: membership and timely premium-call response.
sourceNote: Verified via S.C. Code 38-75-330 (association created; members) and SC Wind & Hail Association Annual Call for Premium. Current 2025 code as of 2026.

title: Mississippi Windstorm Association assessable-insurer participation & assessment
requirement: Licensed property insurers in Mississippi are assessable insurers of the Mississippi Windstorm Underwriting Association (coastal wind/hail residual market), obligated to pay regular assessments per their percentage of participation (their prior-year MS net direct premiums over aggregate assessable-insurer premiums). Members report premium annually. Pass condition: participation and timely assessment payment.
sourceNote: Verified via Miss. Code 83-34-3 (creation; assessable insurers) and Ch. 34; independent entity since 2007. Current 2024 code as of 2026.

title: Alabama Insurance Underwriting Association (Beach Pool) mandatory membership & assessment
requirement: Insurers writing property insurance in Alabama participate in the Alabama Insurance Underwriting Association (coastal Beach Pool for Baldwin and Mobile counties), sharing profits, losses and expenses per the Plan of Operation and subject to assessment on their participation. Members report premium. Pass condition: membership/participation and timely assessment payment.
sourceNote: Verified via Ala. Code 27-1-24 (Alabama Insurance Underwriting Association) and ALDOI coastal materials; association organized 1970. Current 2024 code as of 2026.

title: Colorado FAIR Plan mandatory membership, participation reporting & assessment
requirement: Admitted insurers writing property/commercial property insurance in Colorado must participate in the FAIR Plan Association and share expenses, income and losses on a fair and equitable basis by written premium. Members must submit information annually via the FAIR Plan carrier portal to set participation percentages and are subject to assessment (recoupable via a five-year premium surcharge). Pass condition: participation and timely portal reporting.
sourceNote: Verified via C.R.S. 10-4-1804/1806 (Part 18, from HB23-1288); CO FAIR Plan began issuing policies 2025. Current as of 2026.

title: Connecticut FAIR Plan mandatory subscription, participation & loss sharing
requirement: All insurers licensed to write the lines covered by the Connecticut FAIR Plan must subscribe to and participate in the residual-market joint underwriting organization when the Commissioner approves the plan; participating companies assume the FAIR Plan's liability and share losses/expenses per their participation, reporting premium. Pass condition: subscription/participation and timely premium reporting.
sourceNote: Verified via C.G.S. 38a-329 (residual market mechanism, mandatory subscription) and CID regs sections 38a-328-1 et seq. Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services
regime: Michigan Basic Property Insurance Association (FAIR Plan)
title: Michigan Basic Property Insurance Association (Pool) mandatory membership & assessment
requirement: All insurers authorized to write kinds of insurance included in basic property/home insurance in Michigan must maintain membership in the Michigan Basic Property Insurance Association (Pool); participating members share collectively and pay assessments (recovered through voluntary-market rate adjustments), and must submit assessable-premium calculations online each year. Pass condition: membership and timely assessable-premium reporting/assessment.
sourceNote: Verified via MCL 500.2920 (MBPIA / Pool membership) and MI DIFS; online assessable-premium reporting via MBPIA since Jan 1, 2022. Current as of 2026.

regime: CA Electronic Evidence of Insurance Reporting Program
title: Electronic reporting of private-passenger and commercial/fleet auto policies to CA DMV
requirement: Insurers must electronically report issuance, transfer and termination of private-passenger liability policies, and (since 1/1/2023) commercial and fleet policies by named insured, to the California DMV so it can monitor continuous coverage and suspend registrations. Terminations/changes must be reported within 45 days and new coverage within 30 days.
sourceNote: Verified on CA DMV Electronic Insurance Reporting pages; commercial/fleet expansion effective 1/1/2023; program current as of 2026

regulatorName: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles / Texas Department of Insurance
title: Twice-monthly book-of-business policy reporting to TexasSure
requirement: Every licensed Texas auto liability insurer must report its book of business of active liability policies to the TexasSure Financial Responsibility Verification Program twice each month so registered vehicles can be matched against active coverage. Data is surfaced to law enforcement and registration offices via TLETS.
citation: Tex. Transp. Code Ch. 601, Subch. N
sourceNote: Verified on TxDMV TexasSure page; reporting twice monthly required; current as of 2026

title: Salvage/nonrepairable vehicle title application on auto total-loss settlement
requirement: An insurer that acquires ownership of a motor vehicle through a total-loss claim settlement in Texas must apply to TxDMV for a salvage or nonrepairable vehicle title within 30 days. This surrenders the original title and brands the vehicle in the state title system.
sourceNote: Verified against Tex. Transp. Code Ch. 501 and TxDMV Salvage/Nonrepairable Motor Vehicle Manual (Jan 2026); 30-day duty current

regulatorName: Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles
title: Electronic reporting of PIP and PDL policy initiation and termination to FLHSMV
requirement: All licensed insurers must electronically report the initiation and termination of Personal Injury Protection (PIP) and Property Damage Liability (PDL) coverage to FLHSMV through the Florida Automobile Insurance Verification System so lapses trigger FR7 driver-license/registration suspensions. Insurers must also answer electronic verification requests within 30 days.
sourceNote: Verified on FLHSMV Insurance and No-Fault procedures manual; continuous PIP/PDL reporting current as of 2026

regulatorName: Michigan Catastrophic Claims Association / Dept. of Insurance and Financial Services
title: Annual MCCA assessable-exposure report and premium remittance
requirement: Every insurer writing Michigan no-fault (PIP) coverage is a mandatory MCCA member and must file the MCCA Annual Assessment Determination (Form FIS 0075) reporting Michigan written premium / assessable-exposure data via the MCCA Membership System and remit the per-vehicle catastrophic-claims assessment. The 2025-2026 assessment period runs 7/1/2025-6/30/2026.
sourceNote: Verified against MCL 500.3104 and DIFS/MCCA FIS 0075 form; MMS filing opens July 2026 for the 7/1/2025-6/30/2026 period

regulatorName: NJ Property-Liability Insurance Guaranty Association (UCJF administrator)
regime: NJ Unsatisfied Claim and Judgment Fund (UCJF)
title: UCJF excess-PIP medical benefits first-notice and reimbursement reporting
requirement: A NJ auto liability insurer must notify the Unsatisfied Claim and Judgment Fund (administered by PLIGA) on UCJF Form 1 whenever it has paid $50,000 in PIP medical expense benefits to one person in one accident and potential exposure exceeds $75,000, file a supplemental notice within 90 days, and file Form 3 each quarter thereafter to seek reimbursement.
sourceNote: Verified on NJ DOBI UCJF pages and PLIGA UCJF materials; $50k/$75k thresholds and Form 1/Form 3 cadence current as of 2026

regime: NJ Unsatisfied Claim and Judgment Fund (UCJF)
title: UCJF member-company assessment on NJ auto insurance writings
requirement: Insurers writing automobile insurance in New Jersey are subject to assessment by the UCJF (administered by PLIGA) to fund payment of damages to victims of hit-and-run and uninsured-motorist accidents; these assessments cannot be recovered through policy surcharges.
sourceNote: Verified on PLIGA/NJ DOBI UCJF pages; assessment authority current as of 2026

regulatorName: New York State Department of Financial Services
title: No-fault claim verification and 30-day PIP benefit determination duty
requirement: Under Regulation 68, a NY no-fault insurer must process PIP claims on the prescribed forms, request verification of submitted proof of claim, and pay or deny first-party no-fault benefits within 30 calendar days of receiving proof of claim (benefits are overdue thereafter). Health-service claims must be honored when submitted within 45 days of service.
sourceNote: Verified against DFS full text of 11 NYCRR 65; current consolidated text posted 2024, in force 2026

regulatorName: Georgia Department of Revenue - Motor Vehicle Division
title: Electronic policy reporting to GEICS within 30 days of coverage
requirement: Insurers issuing motor-vehicle liability policies in Georgia must register with a valid NAIC number and electronically report each policy to the Georgia Electronic Insurance Compliance System within 30 days of the coverage start date, plus terminations and vehicle additions/deletions, for VIN cross-reference against the DRIVES title/registration database.
sourceNote: Verified on GA DOR GEICS insurer-responsibilities page (HB 191, 2003); 30-day reporting current as of 2026

regime: VA Verification of Motor Vehicle Insurance
title: Electronic liability-policy change reporting to VA DMV within 30 days
requirement: Insurers licensed in Virginia must electronically report each liability-policy change for a Virginia-registered vehicle to the DMV within 30 days - issuance, cancellation, lapse, reinstatement, or vehicle addition - so DMV can verify continuous coverage and suspend licenses/plates for uninsured vehicles.
sourceNote: Verified against Va. Code 46.2-706.1 and 46.2-706; 30-day electronic reporting current as of 2026

regulatorName: Arizona Department of Transportation - Motor Vehicle Division
title: Auto policy reporting to AZIVS at least every seven days
requirement: Each insurer authorized to sell motor-vehicle liability insurance in Arizona must register with the Arizona Insurance Verification System (AZIVS, live since 6/7/2022) and report new issuances, renewals and cancellations in the format and schedule set by ADOT - at least every seven days - or face civil penalties up to $250/day and possible certificate-of-authority suspension.
sourceNote: Verified against A.R.S. 28-4148 and ADOT/DIFI AZIVS transition notices; AZIVS effective 6/7/2022, current 2026

regulatorName: Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles
title: Auto policy reporting to the Colorado MIIDB designated agent
requirement: Insurers must electronically report motor-vehicle liability policy information to the designated agent of Colorado's Motorist Insurance Identification Database so the state can verify compliance with mandatory coverage; the database is updated from insurer submissions per section 10-4-615, C.R.S.
sourceNote: Verified against C.R.S. 42-7-604 and CO DMV MIIDB page; 1 CCR 204-10-7 rules; current as of 2026

regime: James Lee Atwood Jr. Law / Electronic Insurance Verification System (EIVS)
title: Auto policy reporting to Tennessee EIVS (James Lee Atwood Jr. Law)
requirement: Insurers must participate in Tennessee's online Electronic Insurance Verification System under the James Lee Atwood Jr. Law, providing coverage-status data used to identify uninsured motorists and issue noncompliance notices and penalties under the Financial Responsibility Law of 1977.
sourceNote: Verified against Tenn. Code Ann. 55-12-201 et seq. (enacted 2015) and TN DOR EIVS guidance; current as of 2026

title: Electronic filing of SR22/SR26/SR50 and Certificate of Compliance to Indiana BMV
requirement: Insurers must electronically file proofs of financial responsibility (SR22, SR26, SR50 and Certificate of Compliance) with the Indiana BMV through the Electronic Insurance Forms Submission program; a Certificate of Compliance must be filed within the statutory window after a BMV verification request to update the driver's record.
sourceNote: Verified on Indiana BMV EIFS FAQ; Ind. Code 9-25 financial-responsibility filings; current as of 2026

regulatorName: Louisiana Dept. of Public Safety - Office of Motor Vehicles
title: Monthly book-of-business reporting to LAIVS
requirement: All insurers writing private-passenger and commercial motor-vehicle policies in Louisiana must submit book-of-business (BOB) data to the Louisiana Insurance Verification System at least once per calendar month (weekly if they do not host a VIN-broadcasting web service), used to route real-time verification queries.
sourceNote: Verified against La. R.S. 32:863.2(F) and LAIVS Insurer Reporting Guide v1.1 (2023); current as of 2026

title: Real-time OIVS coverage verification support and 6-month data retention
requirement: As a condition of writing Alabama auto liability policies, an insurer must implement web-services processes that let the OIVS verify policy status in real time and must retain the data needed to verify insurance status for at least six months per IICMVA recommendations.
sourceNote: Verified against Ala. Code 32-7A-9 through 32-7A-11 and AL DOR OIVS User Guide; OIVS live since 1/1/2013, current 2026

title: Mandatory participation in OCIVS real-time verification
requirement: As a condition of writing motor-vehicle policies in Oklahoma, an insurer must participate in the Oklahoma Compulsory Insurance Verification System, cooperating with the Insurance Department to establish and maintain the system and providing real-time policy-status access via web portal.
sourceNote: Verified against 47 O.S. 7-600.2; OCIVS in production since 7/1/2009, transferred to OID by 1/1/2018; current 2026

regulatorName: Utah Department of Public Safety (designated agent)
title: Twice-monthly policy reporting to the Utah UID database
requirement: Insurers issuing Utah motor-vehicle liability, UM/UIM or PIP coverage must provide records of each in-force policy on vehicles registered or garaged in Utah to the DPS designated agent before the 7th and the 21st of each calendar month for the Uninsured Motorist Identification Database.
sourceNote: Verified against Utah Code 41-12a-803 (twice-monthly, before 7th/21st); current as of 2026

title: Monthly liability-policy record reporting to Nevada DMV (NevadaIVS)
requirement: On or before the 15th of each month, each insurer that has written a Nevada motor-vehicle liability policy must provide the DMV a record of each policy issued, amended or terminated in the prior month via the NevadaIVS/Nevada LIVE system, and must give advance notice of system downtime.
sourceNote: Verified against NRS Chapter 485 and Nevada LIVE/NevadaIVS specs; monthly-by-15th reporting current as of 2026

title: Online insurance verification participation and 20-day verification response
requirement: Insurers authorized to issue required Wyoming coverage must cooperate in establishing and maintaining WYDOT's 24/7 online insurance verification system and must verify the existence of an auto liability policy in the approved form within 20 days of a department request.
sourceNote: Verified against Wyo. Stat. 31-4-103(e) and 31-8-203; online verification + 20-day response current as of 2026

regime: Mississippi Motor Vehicle Insurance Verification System (MVIVS)
title: Cooperation and data transfer to Mississippi MVIVS
requirement: Every insurer must cooperate with the Department of Public Safety and Insurance Department to establish and maintain the Motor Vehicle Insurance Verification System, providing liability policy status/information via web services (or file transfer for low-volume insurers) for 24/7 real-time verification.
sourceNote: Verified against Miss. Code 63-16-3/63-16-5; MVIVS established under Ch. 63-16; current as of 2026

title: Monthly personal-auto policy record reporting to Kentucky AVIS
requirement: Each insurer licensed to sell personal-lines motor-vehicle liability insurance in Kentucky must submit to the Transportation Cabinet a monthly record of each vehicle covered by a personal-lines policy for the AVIS database, and must report cancellations for commercial/fleet policies, per 806 KAR 39:070.
sourceNote: Verified against 806 KAR 39:070 and KY DOI KentuckyIVS guide; monthly AVIS reporting current as of 2026

title: Monthly reporting of canceled, terminated and new auto policies to NM MVD
requirement: Insurance carriers must report canceled, terminated and newly issued motor-vehicle insurance policies each month to the New Mexico MVD for the Insurance Identification Database; the MVD notifies the Superintendent of Insurance when a carrier fails to file its monthly report.
sourceNote: Verified against NMSA 66-5-205/66-5-205.1; monthly carrier reporting current as of 2026

regulatorName: South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles
title: Daily compliance and as-needed cancellation reporting to SC ALIR
requirement: Insurers licensed to write auto liability insurance in South Carolina must submit coverage-compliance transactions daily (or as they occur) and cancellation transactions as-needed through the SC ALIR system, which DMV cross-references to driver/vehicle records to identify uninsured registered vehicles.
sourceNote: Verified against S.C. Code Title 56 Ch. 10 and SC DMV ALIR reporting rules; daily/as-needed cadence current as of 2026

regulatorName: South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles
title: Collection and remittance of uninsured-motorist coverage fee to SC UM Fund
requirement: Insurers writing SC auto policies participate in the Uninsured Motorists Fund mechanism whereby the $2 yearly UM-coverage charge is allocated ($1.20 to the State Highway Fund, $0.80 to the Uninsured Enforcement Fund) and remitted for deposit with the State Treasurer.
sourceNote: Verified against S.C. Code 56-10-552 and Title 38 Ch. 77; UM Fund allocation current as of 2026

title: Information Security Program & 72-hour Breach Notice to Commissioner (Alabama)

Passes if the ISP is documented and event notifications are filed within 72 hours.
sourceNote: Verified in NAIC ST-668 state page (Summer 2025), Model Adoption column; Alabama enacted 2019, effective 2019.
