regulatorName: New York State Department of Financial Services
title: Best-Interest standard of care & supervision for annuity and life sales (Reg 187)
requirement: Insurers and producers must act in the best interest of the consumer when recommending an annuity or life insurance product, meeting care/disclosure/conflict/documentation duties, and insurers must maintain a supervision program to ensure producer compliance. Applies to annuity transactions since Aug 1, 2019 and life insurance transactions since Feb 1, 2020. Pass condition: documented best-interest recommendation plus a functioning supervision system.
sourceNote: Verified on NY DFS; First Amendment to Reg 187 in force, upheld as constitutional by NY Court of Appeals 2022; annuities eff. 8/1/2019, life eff. 2/1/2020.

title: Best-Interest annuity recommendation & training standard (SB 263)
requirement: For annuity recommendations made on or after Jan 1, 2025, producers must act in the best interest of the consumer without placing their or the insurer's financial interest ahead of the consumer's, and insurers must maintain a supervision system. Producers must complete initial 8-hour and pre-renewal 4-hour annuity best-interest training. Pass condition: best-interest recommendation, supervision, and completed training.
citation: Cal. Ins. Code § 10509.914 et seq. (SB 263, Stats. 2024, ch. 2)
sourceNote: Verified via CA Legislative Information; SB 263 signed 2/29/2024, best-interest standard effective 1/1/2025 (CA's route to the NAIC 2020 revision).

title: Best-Interest annuity suitability & disclosure rule (28 TAC §3.9722)
requirement: Producers recommending an annuity must act in the best interest of the consumer, satisfying care/disclosure/conflict/documentation obligations, using the NAIC Model 275 disclosure forms, and insurers must supervise recommendations. Pass condition: documented best-interest recommendation with required disclosures and supervision system in place.
sourceNote: Verified via TDI adopted rule; NAIC Model 275 best-interest revision adopted 10/14/2021, filed with TX SOS 10/18/2021.

regulatorName: Florida Office of Insurance Regulation / Dept. of Financial Services
title: Best-Interest standard in annuity transactions (Fla. Stat. §627.4554)
requirement: An agent recommending an annuity must act in the best interest of the consumer under circumstances known at the time, without placing the agent's or insurer's financial interest ahead of the consumer's, meeting care/disclosure/conflict/documentation duties; insurers must maintain a supervision system. Pass condition: documented best-interest recommendation and supervision.
sourceNote: Verified via Florida Senate statutes; best-interest amendments to §627.4554 effective Jan 1, 2024.

title: Best-Interest annuity recommendation rule (50 Ill. Adm. Code 3120)
requirement: Insurance producers recommending an annuity must act in the best interest of the consumer without placing the producer's or insurer's financial interest ahead of the consumer's, satisfying care/disclosure/conflict/documentation obligations; insurers must supervise recommendations. Pass condition: documented best-interest recommendation and supervision program.
sourceNote: Verified via Illinois JCAR/ILGA; best-interest amendments effective Feb 3, 2023 (47 Ill. Reg. 2312).

title: Best-Interest annuity suitability rule (OAC 3901-6-13)
requirement: Producers recommending an annuity must act in the client's best interest without placing the producer's or insurer's financial interest ahead of the client's, meeting care/disclosure/conflict/documentation obligations and enhanced training; insurers must maintain supervision. Pass condition: documented best-interest recommendation, training, and supervision.
sourceNote: Verified via Ohio Dept. of Insurance; NAIC Model 275 best-interest revision effective Aug 14, 2021.

title: Best-Interest annuity suitability standard (Act 99 of 2021)
requirement: Producers recommending an annuity must act in the best interest of the consumer without placing their own or the insurer's financial interest first, satisfying care/disclosure/conflict/documentation duties and a one-time 4-hour best-interest training; insurers must supervise recommendations. Pass condition: documented best-interest recommendation, training, and supervision.
sourceNote: Verified via PA Insurance Dept.; Act 99 of 2021 signed 12/22/2021, best-interest standard effective June 20, 2022.

regulatorName: Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services
title: Best-Interest annuity suitability standard (MCL 500.4151 et seq.)
requirement: Producers recommending an annuity must act in the best interest of the consumer without placing the producer's or insurer's financial interest ahead of the consumer's, satisfying care/disclosure/conflict/documentation obligations; insurers must maintain a supervision system. Pass condition: documented best-interest recommendation and supervision.
sourceNote: Verified via Michigan Legislature; PA 266 of 2020 signed 12/29/2020, best-interest standard effective June 29, 2021.

regulatorName: Georgia Office of Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire
title: Best-Interest annuity suitability rule (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 120-2-94)
requirement: Anyone recommending an annuity to a Georgia consumer must satisfy the four best-interest conduct obligations — care, disclosure, conflict of interest, and documentation — and insurers must maintain a supervision system. Pass condition: documented best-interest recommendation meeting all four obligations and supervision.
sourceNote: Verified via GA OCI; Rule 120-2-94 best-interest standard effective July 1, 2023.

title: Semi-annual Death Master File comparison for unclaimed life & annuity benefits
requirement: Insurers must compare in-force life insurance policies, annuity contracts, and retained asset accounts against a Death Master File at least semi-annually (full file first, update files thereafter) to identify potential matches, then perform due diligence and pay benefits or locate beneficiaries; no fees may be charged to beneficiaries. Pass condition: documented semi-annual DMF comparisons and timely beneficiary outreach.
citation: Tex. Ins. Code ch. 1109, Subch. A-1 (SB 561, 2017)
sourceNote: Verified via Texas Statutes; Subch. A-1 enacted by SB 561 (2017), requires at-least-semi-annual DMF comparisons.

regime: Unclaimed Life Insurance and Annuities Act (NCOIL model)
title: Death Master File matching & beneficiary outreach for unclaimed life benefits
requirement: Insurers must compare in-force policies, annuity contracts, and retained asset accounts against a Death Master File, validate matches, and use good-faith efforts to confirm death, determine benefits, and locate beneficiaries to provide claim forms and instructions. Pass condition: documented DMF matching and beneficiary location efforts consistent with the Act.
citation: Cal. Ins. Code § 10509.940 et seq. (Art. 12; SB 740, 2019)
sourceNote: Verified via CA Legislative Information; Unclaimed Life Insurance and Annuities Act (SB 740) chaptered 2019.

regime: Unclaimed Life Insurance / DMF search duty
title: Annual Death Master File search & 120-day due diligence for life benefits
requirement: Life insurers must search the SSA Death Master File at least annually (or as often as they check the DMF for annuities) against active and terminated policies back to 1992; on a match, the insurer has 120 days to confirm the death, determine benefits, and use good-faith efforts to locate beneficiaries. Pass condition: documented at-least-annual DMF searches and timely due diligence.
sourceNote: Verified via Florida Statutes ch. 717; DMF search duty added by 2016 amendment, requires at-least-annual searches and 120-day due diligence.

regulatorName: New York State Department of Financial Services
title: Death-index comparison & unclaimed benefit payment (Ins. Law §3240)
requirement: Insurers must compare in-force life insurance policies, annuity contracts, and retained asset accounts against the SSA death master file (or an equivalent acceptable to the superintendent) to identify deceased insureds, then locate and pay beneficiaries; the superintendent maintains a Lost Policy Finder consumers may use. Pass condition: documented death-index comparisons and beneficiary payment/outreach.
sourceNote: Verified via NY Senate / NY DFS; §3240 governs unclaimed benefits, death-index matching, and the DFS Lost Policy Finder.

regime: Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act (NCOIL model)
title: Semi-annual Death Master File comparison for unclaimed life benefits
requirement: Insurers must perform an initial full Death Master File comparison and thereafter compare in-force policies, annuity contracts, and retained asset accounts against DMF update files at least semi-annually to identify matches, then locate beneficiaries and pay benefits; no fees may be charged to beneficiaries. Pass condition: documented semi-annual DMF comparisons and beneficiary outreach.
sourceNote: Verified via Illinois General Assembly; Act requires at-least-semi-annual DMF comparisons, initial full-file comparison due by 12/31/2017 (DMF duty effective 1/1/2017).

regulatorName: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
title: Death-index comparison & Lost Policy Finder for unclaimed life benefits
requirement: Insurers must compare in-force life insurance policies, annuity contracts, and retained asset accounts against the SSA death master file (or equivalent acceptable to the commissioner) to identify deceased insureds and locate beneficiaries; the commissioner maintains a Lost Policy Finder via secure online portal and mail. Pass condition: documented death-index comparisons and beneficiary outreach.
sourceNote: Verified via NJ Legislature; P.L. 2017, c.236 supplements Title 17B with DMF/death-index matching and a Lost Policy Finder.

regime: Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits / DMF search duty
title: Semi-annual DMF comparison with 90-day match due diligence
requirement: Insurers must compare in-force life insurance policies, annuity contracts, and retained asset accounts against the Death Master File at least semi-annually; on a match they must within 90 days confirm the death, determine whether benefits are due, and use good-faith efforts to locate beneficiaries and provide claim forms. Pass condition: documented semi-annual DMF comparisons and 90-day due diligence.
sourceNote: Verified via Maryland Insurance Article §16-118 (Failure to Search Death Master File); requires at-least-semi-annual comparisons and 90-day match follow-up.

title: One-Year Wildfire Non-Renewal/Cancellation Moratorium Compliance (Ins. Code 675.1)
requirement: After the Governor declares a wildfire state of emergency, an insurer must not cancel or non-renew residential property insurance for any risk located within or adjacent to the fire perimeter ZIP codes, for one year from the declaration date, based on wildfire risk or an actual wildfire loss. Applies to all residential policyholders in affected ZIP codes (including those with no loss); since Jan 1, 2026 SB 547 extends comparable protection to commercial lines. Pass condition: no prohibited non-renewals in listed ZIPs during the moratorium window.
sourceNote: Verified on CDI catastrophe moratorium page + CDI Bulletin 2025-13; SB 824 (2018), commercial extension SB 547 effective Jan 1, 2026. Current as of July 2026.

regime: Safer from Wildfires (Mitigation in Rating Plans)
title: Wildfire Mitigation Discount / Safer from Wildfires Rating-Plan Compliance (10 CCR 2644.9)
requirement: A homeowners insurer that offers any price variation based on wildfire risk must incorporate into its rating plan mitigation credits/discounts for the recognized 'Safer from Wildfires' measures across the three layers (structure, immediate surroundings, community, including Fire Risk Reduction Communities and Firewise USA sites in good standing). Insurers must apply the differentials and disclose available discounts to policyholders. Pass condition: an approved rating plan reflecting the mandated mitigation factors.
sourceNote: Verified via CDI 'Mitigation in Rating Plans and Wildfire Risk Models' FAQ + 10 CCR 2644.9; effective Oct 14, 2022, compliance within 180 days. Current as of July 2026.

regime: Sustainable Insurance Strategy - Net Cost of Reinsurance
title: Standard Net Cost of Reinsurance in Ratemaking Filing Compliance (10 CCR 2644.25.2)
requirement: An insurer electing to include net cost of reinsurance in a homeowners/property rate application must use the Commissioner's Standard NCOR parameters (permitted return multiples by loss-probability layer), use the same catastrophe model here as under 10 CCR 2644.4.5, adjust for defense/cost-containment, and make required model information public. Availability of NCOR/cat-model rate treatment is conditioned on writing commitments in distressed/wildfire-prone areas. Pass condition: a compliant rate filing meeting the SIS coverage commitments.
sourceNote: Verified via 10 CCR 2644.25.2 (Cornell LII) + CDI Sustainable Insurance Strategy page; effective Jan 13, 2025, first NCOR/cat-model homeowners filings approved 2025.

regime: Sustainable Insurance Strategy - Cat Model Consistency
title: Wildfire Catastrophe Model Disclosure & Single-Model Consistency in Rate Filings (10 CCR 2644.4.5)
requirement: An insurer using a Department-reviewed wildfire catastrophe model in a rate application must satisfy the model governance requirements of 10 CCR 2644.4.5(d)-(f), use the same model for both loss projection and net-cost-of-reinsurance (no 'model shopping'), and make required model information public in the filing. Pass condition: consistent, disclosed cat-model use accepted in the prior-approval rate review.
sourceNote: Verified via CDI Catastrophe Model Form + SIS materials referencing 2644.4.5 subdivisions (d)-(f); part of 2024-2025 SIS rulemaking. Current as of July 2026.

title: Wildfire Total-Loss Personal Property Advance Payment Without Inventory (Ins. Code 10103.7)
requirement: On a total loss of a home in a declared state of emergency, the insurer must pay contents/personal property coverage without requiring an itemized inventory up to a statutory minimum, raised effective Jan 1, 2026 from 30% to 60% of the personal property limit (or up to $350,000), and must permit combining dwelling and other-structures limits. Pass condition: advance payment issued at the statutory floor upon a covered total loss without demanding an inventory first.
sourceNote: Verified via CA Legislative Information Ins. Code 10103.7; 60%/$350,000 floor effective Jan 1, 2026 (SB 49). Current as of July 2026.

title: Hurricane/Windstorm Mitigation Credit Rate Filing & Website Disclosure (Fla. Stat. 627.0629)
requirement: A residential property insurer's rate filing must include actuarially reasonable discounts, credits, or deductible reductions for construction features that reduce windstorm loss (roof strength/covering, roof-to-wall, opening protection, etc.), reflecting the full actuarial value determined by OIR. Effective Oct 1, 2023 each such insurer must also publish on its website a description of the hurricane mitigation discounts available. Pass condition: filed mitigation differentials plus the required web disclosure.
sourceNote: Verified via Florida Statutes 627.0629 (2025); website-disclosure duty effective Oct 1, 2023. Current as of July 2026.

title: Residential Property Claim: 7-Day Acknowledge / 60-Day Pay-or-Deny (Fla. Stat. 627.70131)
requirement: On a residential property claim the insurer must acknowledge any claim communication within 7 calendar days (627.70131(1)(a)), begin the reasonably necessary investigation within 7 days of receiving proof-of-loss (627.70131(3)(a)), and pay or deny the initial, reopened, or supplemental claim within 60 days of notice (627.70131(7)(a)) absent factors beyond its control; late payments accrue statutory interest. Pass condition: all three deadlines met per claim.
sourceNote: Verified via Florida Statutes 627.70131 (2023, subsections (1)(a)/(3)(a)/(7)(a)); 60-day pay-or-deny per SB 2-A (Dec 2022). Current as of July 2026.

title: Hurricane Deductible Offer & Recurring Disclosure Notice (Fla. Stat. 627.701)
requirement: Before issuing personal-lines residential property coverage the insurer must offer hurricane deductible options ($500, 2%, 5%, 10% of dwelling limit), provide a hurricane-deductible availability notice on an OIR-approved form at each renewal and at least once every three years, and obtain the prescribed handwritten signed statement when the insured elects a higher deductible. Pass condition: documented offer, recurring notice, and signed election where applicable.
sourceNote: Verified via Florida Statutes 627.701 (2024); offer options and 3-year/renewal notice requirements. Current as of July 2026.

regulatorName: State Board of Administration - Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund
title: Mandatory FHCF Reimbursement Contract Execution & Annual Data Call (Fla. Stat. 215.555)
requirement: Every residential property insurer writing in Florida must participate in the Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund by executing the annual reimbursement contract with the SBA and reporting its covered exposure and loss data through the FHCF annual data call. Pass condition: signed reimbursement contract on file and timely, accurate data-call submission each contract year.
sourceNote: Verified via FHCF (SBA) 'About the FHCF' and FHCF annual data call materials; mandatory participation under s. 215.555. Current as of July 2026.

regulatorName: Citizens Property Insurance Corporation / Florida OIR
title: Citizens Eligibility Screening Against Private-Market Offer Threshold (Fla. Stat. 627.351(6))
requirement: An applicant is ineligible for Citizens if an authorized insurer offers comparable coverage at or below the statutory eligibility threshold; a private carrier's offer at/under the premium threshold in s. 627.351(6)(c)5.a. disqualifies new Citizens coverage. Carriers participating in take-out/clearinghouse must screen and, where they make a qualifying offer, trigger Citizens ineligibility. Pass condition: eligibility determined against the offer threshold and documented.
sourceNote: Verified via Florida Statutes 627.351(6) (2024) incl. (c)5.a. offer-threshold eligibility. Current as of July 2026.

regime: Texas Prompt Payment of Claims Act
title: Property/Hail-Wind Claim Prompt-Handling: 15-Day Acknowledge, Accept/Reject, 5-Day Pay (Tex. Ins. Code Ch. 542)
requirement: On a first-party property claim (including hail/windstorm) the insurer must acknowledge receipt, begin investigation, and request needed items within 15 days; notify acceptance or rejection within 15 business days of receiving all required proof-of-loss items (extendable 45 days); and, if accepted, pay within 5 business days (20 for surplus lines). Non-compliance triggers 18% annual interest plus attorney's fees. Pass condition: each deadline met per claim.
citation: Tex. Ins. Code Ch. 542, Subch. B (542.055-.058)
sourceNote: Verified via Texas Insurance Code Chapter 542, Subchapter B (Prompt Payment of Claims); 18% penalty under 542.060. Current as of July 2026.

regulatorName: Texas Department of Insurance / Texas Windstorm Insurance Association
title: TWIA Windstorm Eligibility: WPI-8 Certificate of Compliance Verification (Tex. Ins. Code Ch. 2210)
requirement: To bind or renew TWIA windstorm/hail coverage on a structure in the 14 designated coastal counties (and designated Harris County areas), the property must have a WPI-8 Certificate of Compliance (or equivalent) evidencing windstorm-code inspection of new construction/re-roofs; uncertified 1988-2009 structures require a 15% surcharge. Pass condition: valid WPI-8 (or surcharge) on file before coverage is issued.
sourceNote: Verified via TWIA windstorm-certification page + Texas Insurance Code Ch. 2210 and TDI windstorm inspection program. Current as of July 2026.

regulatorName: Texas Windstorm Insurance Association / Texas Department of Insurance
title: TWIA Member-Insurer Assessment Participation & Take-Out Data Reporting (Tex. Ins. Code 2210.613 / 2210.701)
requirement: Every property insurer authorized to write windstorm/hail in Texas is a TWIA member subject to assessment when TWIA cannot meet its Class 2 public-security obligations (2210.613); insurers assuming policies through the depopulation/assumption-reinsurance program (2210.701) must report premium and loss transactions on assumed policies from the assumption date. Pass condition: assessments paid when levied and accurate transfer-date reporting on assumed business.
sourceNote: Verified via Texas Insurance Code Ch. 2210 (2210.613 assessments; 2210.701 depopulation) + TWIA depopulation reporting rules. Current as of July 2026.

title: Commercial Certificate-of-Insurance Form Filing & Approval (Tex. Ins. Code Ch. 1811)
requirement: A property/casualty insurer or agent may not deliver a certificate of insurance in Texas unless the certificate form has been filed with and approved by TDI, and may not issue a certificate that alters/amends/extends policy coverage or conveys contractual rights inconsistent with the policy. Pass condition: only TDI-approved certificate forms are used and no coverage-altering language is issued.
sourceNote: Verified via Texas Insurance Code Ch. 1811 (Certificates of Property and Casualty Insurance) + TDI certificates FAQ. Current as of July 2026.

regulatorName: New York State Department of Financial Services
title: Hurricane Deductible Trigger Standard & Uniform Disclosure Notice (N.Y. Ins. Law 3445)
requirement: For homeowners and dwelling-fire personal-lines policies, a hurricane deductible may be triggered only when the meteorological entity determines a hurricane made landfall in New York, applying to wind damage in a defined landfall window, and the insurer must provide the DFS-prescribed plain-language notice explaining the deductible amount and when it applies. Under the DFS regulation effective Feb 2, 2026 insurers may seek hurricane deductibles statewide subject to these standards. Pass condition: compliant trigger terms and required notice.
sourceNote: Verified via N.Y. Insurance Law 3445 + DFS uniform hurricane-deductible regulation effective Feb 2, 2026. Current as of July 2026.

regulatorName: New York State Department of Financial Services
regime: NY Regulation 64 - Unfair Claims Settlement Practices
title: Property Claim Handling: 15-Business-Day Acknowledge, Investigate & Accept/Reject (11 NYCRR 216)
requirement: On a property claim the insurer must acknowledge the claim within 15 business days of notice, commence investigation and furnish the list of required proof-of-loss items within 15 business days, and advise acceptance or rejection in writing within 15 business days of receiving a properly executed proof of loss (30 business days if arson is suspected). Pass condition: each Regulation 64 timeframe met.
sourceNote: Verified via 11 NYCRR Part 216 (Regulation 64) and DFS Insurance Law 2601. Current as of July 2026.

regulatorName: New York State Department of Financial Services
regime: NY Certificates of Insurance (Insurance Law Article 5)
title: Compliant Commercial Certificate-of-Insurance Issuance (N.Y. Ins. Law 501-502)
requirement: An insurer or producer must issue certificates of insurance only on forms promulgated by the issuing insurer or an approved industry-standard form, and may not issue a certificate that is false, misleading, or that purports to alter, amend, or extend the coverage or terms of the referenced policy. Pass condition: only compliant, approved-form certificates are issued for commercial insureds.
sourceNote: Verified via NY DFS certificates-of-insurance guidance + N.Y. Insurance Law Article 5 (enacted 2014). Current as of July 2026.

regulatorName: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
title: Hurricane Deductible Trigger Uniformity & Policy Disclosure (NJDOBI Bulletin 02-11)
requirement: An insurer using a hurricane or named-storm deductible on homeowners policies must follow the department's uniform trigger standard (hurricane deductible applies only when a storm is declared a hurricane and the specified sustained-wind threshold is met in the state), state the deductible's timing clearly on the policy, and provide the required consumer notice with a practical example. Pass condition: uniform trigger language and disclosure on file.
sourceNote: Verified via NJDOBI Bulletin 02-11 and NJDOBI extreme-weather consumer guidance on hurricane-deductible trigger/disclosure. Current as of July 2026.

regime: LA Payment & Adjustment of Claims (Good Faith Duty)
title: Property Claim: 14-Day Initiate (30-Day Catastrophe) & 30-Day Pay After Proof of Loss (La. R.S. 22:1892)
requirement: An insurer must begin loss adjustment of a property-damage claim within 14 days of notice (30 days for a catastrophic loss, extendable up to 30 additional days by the Commissioner during a declared disaster) and pay the amount due within 30 days after receiving satisfactory proof of loss; arbitrary, capricious, or bad-faith failure exposes the insurer to statutory penalties. Pass condition: adjustment initiated and payment made within the statutory periods.
sourceNote: Verified via Louisiana R.S. 22:1892 (payment/adjustment of claims; good-faith duty) on the LA State Legislature site. Current as of July 2026.

title: Texas Statistical Plan Residential Property Data Reporting (28 TAC Ch. 5)
requirement: Insurers writing residential property in Texas must report premium and loss statistical data for coastal and non-coastal residential risks to the designated statistical agent under the Texas Statistical Plan for Residential Risks, supporting TDI/TWIA ratemaking and coastal exposure monitoring. Pass condition: complete, accurate statistical-plan data submitted on the prescribed schedule.
citation: 28 TAC Ch. 5 (Texas Statistical Plan for Residential Risks)
sourceNote: Verified via TDI Texas Statistical Plan for Residential Risks (28 TAC Ch. 5). Current as of July 2026.

regime: FL Property Insurance Reform - Mediation/Arbitration Notice
title: Mandatory Mediation Program Notice & Binding-Arbitration Endorsement Rules (Fla. Stat. 627.7015 / SB 2-A)
requirement: On a first-party residential property claim the insurer must notify the policyholder of the state mandatory mediation program at issuance/renewal and when a claim is filed; if the insurer requires binding arbitration, it must attach a separate endorsement, provide an actuarially sound premium credit, and obtain the insured's signed election. Pass condition: mediation notice delivered and, where used, a compliant arbitration endorsement with signed election.
sourceNote: Verified via Florida Senate SB 2-A (2022A) bill summary re mediation notice and binding-arbitration endorsement; codified at s. 627.7015. Current as of July 2026.

title: California FAIR Plan Membership, Assessment & Clearinghouse Offer Duties (Ins. Code 10091-10095.5)
requirement: Every insurer admitted to write basic property insurance in California must be a FAIR Plan member, participate in FAIR Plan assessments when levied by the Commissioner, and, when making a voluntary offer through the residential clearinghouse, honor the policyholder's existing producer relationship. Pass condition: membership maintained, approved assessments paid, and clearinghouse offer rules followed.
sourceNote: Verified via CDI FAIR Plan expansion release (2025) + Assembly Insurance Committee FAIR Plan clearinghouse materials; membership/assessment under Ins. Code 10091 et seq. Current as of July 2026.

regulatorName: Virginia Department of Health / Virginia Health Information
title: Virginia APCD paid-claims data submission for insurers/HMOs (1,000+ lives)
requirement: Issuers of individual or group accident and sickness policies and HMOs covering at least 1,000 Virginia lives, plus TPAs for non-ERISA groups, must submit eligibility, medical and pharmacy paid-claims files to the Virginia All-Payer Claims Database. Submission is mandatory on the schedule set by VDH/VHI. Fully-insured commercial coverage is in scope.
sourceNote: Verified on Virginia Law site; statute originally enacted 2012, mandatory submitter scope expanded by SB 1216 effective July 1, 2019; ERISA self-funded plans exempt per § 32.1-276.7:1(P) (Gobeille), voluntary opt-in only. Current as of 2026.

title: HealthFacts RI APCD data submission for payers with 3,000+ covered lives
requirement: Commercial health plans and insurers with more than 3,000 covered lives in Rhode Island must regularly submit member eligibility, medical and pharmacy claim files to the HealthFacts RI All-Payer Claims Database, with member opt-out honored. Submission is mandatory per DOH regulation.
sourceNote: Verified on RI Secretary of State rules portal and RIDOH; APCD collecting since 2014, threshold 3,000+ covered lives. ERISA self-funded not compelled (Gobeille). Current as of 2026.

title: Delaware Health Care Claims Database submission for health insurers
requirement: Any health insurer providing health-care coverage to a Delaware resident is a Mandatory Reporting Entity and must submit member eligibility, medical services claims and pharmacy claims to the Delaware Health Care Claims Database per the DHIN Submission Guide. Submission is mandatory.
sourceNote: Verified on Delaware Code and legis.delaware.gov; SB 227 signed Aug 29, 2018 expanded mandatory reporting entities to health insurers. ERISA self-funded not compelled (Gobeille). Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Washington Office of Financial Management / Health Care Authority
title: WA-APCD claims data submission for health carriers
requirement: Health carriers (and TPAs for non-ERISA groups) must submit medical, pharmacy and eligibility claims data to the Washington State All-Payer Claims Database as data suppliers under the OFM/HCA program and lead-organization rules. Submission is mandatory for in-scope fully-insured commercial coverage.
sourceNote: Verified via APCD Council legislation-by-state (RCW 43.371) and WA HCA; APCD operational, ERISA self-funded voluntary only (Gobeille). Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Nevada Department of Health and Human Services
title: Nevada APCD data submission for insurers covering 1,000+ residents
requirement: Health insurers that cover 1,000 or more Nevada residents must submit claims and enrollment data to the Nevada All-Payer Claims Database on the DHHS-defined schedule. Submission is mandatory for in-scope fully-insured commercial payers.
citation: Nevada APCD program (SB 40, 2021); NAC/NRS APCD provisions
sourceNote: Verified on Nevada APCD state portal (apcd.nv.gov); mandatory for insurers with 1,000+ Nevada residents. ERISA self-funded not compelled (Gobeille). Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: California Department of Managed Health Care / California Department of Insurance
title: SB 855 annual mental-health-parity compliance report to DMHC/CDI
requirement: California-regulated health plans and disability insurers must maintain a parity compliance program and submit annual reporting/analysis demonstrating that MH/SUD medical-necessity criteria, utilization management, and NQTLs comply with California parity law, filed with DMHC or CDI. Pass condition is a compliant, filed annual report.
sourceNote: Verified on leginfo.legislature.ca.gov (SB 855, chaptered 2020) and DMHC; annual parity reporting/compliance obligations effective for plan years beginning Jan 1, 2021. Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: New York State Department of Financial Services
title: Biennial MH/SUD parity report to NY DFS
requirement: Insurers authorized to write accident and health insurance, Article 43 corporations, and MCOs offering commercial products must submit a biennial Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Parity Report to DFS covering the preceding two calendar years, using DFS templates and attestation. Pass condition is a timely, complete biennial filing.
sourceNote: Verified on DFS parity-reporting page; biennial report required beginning July 1, 2019 and every two years thereafter. Current as of 2026.

title: Annual mental-health-parity report/comparative analysis to Illinois DOI
requirement: An insurer that amends, delivers, issues, or renews a group or individual policy covering MH/SUD benefits must submit an annual report to the Illinois Department of Insurance documenting pharmacy management, utilization review, medical-necessity criteria, NQTLs, and comparative analyses demonstrating parity compliance. Pass condition is a timely, complete annual submission.
sourceNote: Verified on Illinois General Assembly (ILCS); subsection (k) requires insurer annual reports starting September 1, 2023 and annually thereafter. Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: California Department of Managed Health Care / California Department of Insurance
title: SB 17 annual prescription-drug cost report to DMHC/CDI
requirement: Health plans and insurers that file rate information with DMHC or CDI must report annually (by October 1) the 25 most frequently prescribed drugs, 25 most costly by plan spend, 25 with the highest year-over-year spend increase, and drug-cost impact on premiums. Pass condition is a timely, complete annual filing.
sourceNote: Verified on leginfo and HCAI/DMHC; health plan/insurer reporting due Oct 1, 2018 and annually thereafter (distinct from manufacturer quarterly reporting to HCAI). Current as of 2026.

title: Carrier/PBM prescription-drug data reporting to Colorado APCD/PDAB
requirement: Each carrier, and each PBM acting on its behalf, must annually report prescription-drug data (drugs dispensed and paid during the preceding calendar year) to the Colorado all-payer health claims database to support Prescription Drug Affordability Board reviews. Pass condition is a timely report with confidential information properly flagged.
sourceNote: Verified on Colorado General Assembly (SB21-175) and DORA DOI; carrier/PBM reporting begins with 2022 calendar-year data, annually thereafter. Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Oregon Department of Consumer and Business Services, Division of Financial Regulation
regime: Oregon Prescription Drug Price Transparency Act
title: Oregon insurer annual prescription-drug price transparency report to DFR
requirement: Health insurers offering a health benefit plan in Oregon must annually report to the Division of Financial Regulation the top 25 drugs (most frequently prescribed, most costly, greatest cost increase) and the effect of prescription-drug costs and rebates on premiums. Pass condition is a timely, complete annual submission.
sourceNote: Verified on Oregon DFR insurers page; annual insurer reporting under ORS 646A.689 / OAR 836-053-1630. Current as of 2026.

title: Washington carrier annual drug-price transparency data submission to HCA
requirement: Health insurance carriers must annually submit drug-cost, rebate and premium-impact data to the Washington Health Care Authority Drug Price Transparency program per the HCA Carrier Data Submission Guide. Pass condition is a timely, complete carrier submission in the required format.
sourceNote: Verified on WA HCA DPT program pages and carrier submission guide; program created 2019, annual carrier reporting under RCW 43.71C. Current as of 2026.

title: Texas PBM annual prescription-drug rebate/fee report to TDI
requirement: Each pharmacy benefit manager (acting for a health benefit plan issuer) must file an annual report with the TDI commissioner by March 1 stating aggregated rebates, fees, price-protection payments and other manufacturer payments collected for the preceding calendar year, without disclosing plan/enrollee or drug-specific identifiers. Pass condition is a timely, compliant filing.
sourceNote: Verified on Texas statutes (Ins. Code ch. 1369, subch. K) and TDI; HB 2536 (86th Leg., 2019), PBM report due March 1 annually. Current as of 2026.

regulatorName: Nevada Department of Health and Human Services
title: Nevada PBM annual essential-diabetes-drug transparency report to DHHS
requirement: Pharmacy benefit managers must annually report to Nevada DHHS the required cost and rebate information on essential diabetes drugs on the state's published lists, subject to trade-secret protections. Pass condition is a timely, complete annual submission; DHHS may impose administrative penalties for failure to report.
sourceNote: Verified on Nevada DHHS drug-transparency pages and NRS 439B; SB 539 (2017), annual PBM/manufacturer reporting on essential diabetes drugs. Current as of 2026.

regime: CA Insurance Information and Privacy Protection Act (IIPPA)
title: Adverse Underwriting Decision written-reason notice under CA IIPPA
requirement: In any adverse underwriting decision (declination, cancellation, nonrenewal, higher-than-standard rate) the insurer or agent must give the applicant/policyholder the specific reasons in writing or notice of the right to request them, plus a summary of privacy rights; written reasons and supporting personal/privileged information must be furnished within 21 business days of a written request made within 90 business days. Pass condition: documented reason notices issued for every individually underwritten adverse decision.
sourceNote: Verified on California Insurance Code Art. 6.6 (791-791.28); long-standing act, in force July 2026 (SB 354 amendments still pending in Appropriations, not yet enacted).

regime: CA Insurance Information and Privacy Protection Act (IIPPA)
title: Insurance information-practices notice and disclosure limits under CA IIPPA
requirement: Insurers, agents and insurance-support organizations must deliver a notice of information practices at or before policy delivery describing what personal information is collected and the circumstances of disclosure, and may not disclose personal or privileged information collected in an insurance transaction to nonaffiliated third parties except within the enumerated statutory exceptions. Pass condition: compliant information-practice notices and disclosure controls in place.
sourceNote: Verified on California Insurance Code Art. 6.6; in force July 2026.

regime: Connecticut Insurance Information and Privacy Protection Act
title: Adverse Underwriting Decision reasons notice under CT IIPPA (Ch. 705)
requirement: For any individually underwritten adverse underwriting decision, the insurer or agent must provide written reasons or a summary of the right to request them and, on written request, furnish the specific reasons and supporting personal/privileged information. Insurers may not base an adverse decision solely on a prior adverse decision or residual-market placement. Pass condition: statutory reason notices issued and prohibited bases avoided.
sourceNote: Verified on CGA Chapter 705 (secs. 38a-975 to 38a-998); in force July 2026.

regime: CID Big Data / Use of Consumer Data Guidance
title: Annual Data (Big Data) Certification filing to the CID by Sept 22
requirement: Licensed insurers using consumer data, algorithms and predictive models must file an annual data certification (by September 22) in which a responsible officer attests to an established process for third-party-derived data, agrees to provide all data used to build models/algorithms to the CID on request, and confirms records will be retained. Pass condition: certification submitted annually via the CID portal.
citation: CID Bulletin No. MC-25 (Use of AI Systems by Insurers) — annual AI/data certification
sourceNote: Verified via CID big-data guidance amended to require annual certification (Day Pitney 2022); annual filing in force July 2026.

regime: Illinois Insurance Information and Privacy Protection (Ins. Code Art. XL)
title: Adverse Underwriting Decision reasons notice under 215 ILCS 5 Art. XL
requirement: On any adverse underwriting decision, the insurer or agent must provide the specific reasons in writing or notice of the right to request them plus a summary of rights, and within 21 business days of a written request (made within 90 business days) furnish the specific reasons and the items of personal/privileged information supporting them. Pass condition: compliant reason notices for all individually underwritten adverse decisions.
sourceNote: Verified on 215 ILCS 5 Article XL (Insurance Information and Privacy Protection); in force July 2026.

regime: MA Insurance Information and Privacy Protection (G.L. c. 175I)
title: Adverse Underwriting Decision notice and information-practices duties under c. 175I
requirement: Insurers must provide a notice of insurance information practices and, on any adverse underwriting decision, give written reasons or notice of the right to request them and disclose supporting personal information (with special handling of medical/mental-health record data). Pass condition: information-practice notices delivered and adverse-decision reason notices issued per c. 175I.
sourceNote: Verified on M.G.L. c. 175I (Insurance Information and Privacy Protection); in force July 2026.

regime: Maine Insurance Information and Privacy Protection Act (Title 24-A Ch. 24)
title: Adverse Underwriting Decision reasons notice under Maine IIPPA
requirement: For any individually underwritten adverse underwriting decision (declination, cancellation, nonrenewal, or adverse change in terms/charge), the insurer or agent must furnish written reasons or notice of the right to request them, and on request supply the specific reasons and supporting personal/privileged information. Pass condition: statutory reason notices issued and prior-decision bases avoided.
sourceNote: Verified on Maine Title 24-A, Chapter 24 (Insurance Information and Privacy Protection Act); in force July 2026.

regulatorName: Arizona Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions
regime: Arizona Insurance Information and Privacy Protection (A.R.S. Title 20 Ch. 11)
title: Adverse Underwriting Decision reasons notice under A.R.S. Title 20 Ch. 11
requirement: On an adverse underwriting decision for individually underwritten life, health, disability, property or casualty coverage, the insurer or producer must provide written reasons or notice of the right to request them, and within 21 business days of a written request furnish supporting information; insurance scores using prohibited factors are barred. Pass condition: compliant reason notices for all adverse decisions.
sourceNote: Verified on Arizona Revised Statutes Title 20, Chapter 11 (secs. 20-2101 et seq.); in force July 2026.

regulatorName: Virginia State Corporation Commission, Bureau of Insurance
regime: Virginia Insurance Information and Privacy Protection (Title 38.2 Ch. 6)
title: Adverse Underwriting Decision notice on Commission-approved form under 38.2-610
requirement: On any adverse underwriting decision the insurer or agent must give written notice, in a form approved by the Commission, of the specific reasons or the right to request them, and on request disclose the supporting personal/privileged information (subject to a fraud exception). Insurers may not base a decision on a prior adverse decision or residual-market placement. Pass condition: approved-form notices issued for all adverse decisions.
sourceNote: Verified on Code of Virginia Title 38.2, Chapter 6; in force July 2026.

regulatorName: Georgia Office of Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire
regime: Georgia Insurance Information Privacy (O.C.G.A. Title 33 Ch. 39)
title: Adverse Underwriting Decision procedure and reasons notice under O.C.G.A. 33-39-11
requirement: On an adverse underwriting decision the insurer or agent must provide written reasons or notice of the right to request them plus a summary of rights, and on a timely written request furnish additional supporting information; oral notice is allowed only when the decision results solely from an oral inquiry. Pass condition: compliant reason notices issued for all adverse decisions.
sourceNote: Verified on Georgia Code Title 33, Chapter 39 (Collection, Use and Disclosure of Information by Insurance Institutions); in force July 2026.

regime: NC Insurance Consumer/Customer Information Privacy (G.S. Ch. 58 Art. 39)
title: Adverse Underwriting Decision reasons notice under N.C.G.S. 58-39-55
requirement: On any adverse underwriting decision the insurer or agent must give written notice, in a form approved by the Commissioner, of the specific reasons or the right to request them plus a summary of rights, and within 21 business days of a written request furnish the reasons and the personal/privileged information supporting them. Pass condition: approved-form reason notices for all individually underwritten adverse decisions.
sourceNote: Verified on North Carolina General Statutes Chapter 58, Article 39; in force July 2026.

regime: Nevada Insurance Privacy of Consumer Financial Information (NAC Ch. 679B)
title: Initial and annual privacy notices to consumers/customers under NAC 679B
requirement: Insurers must deliver an initial privacy notice to each new customer and an annual privacy notice thereafter (while the policy is in force), disclosing the categories of nonpublic personal financial information collected and disclosed and the categories of affiliates and nonaffiliated third parties receiving it, with an opt-out. Pass condition: initial and annual notices delivered per the GLBA-implementing regulation.
sourceNote: Verified on Nevada Administrative Code Chapter 679B (privacy and opt-out notices); in force July 2026.

regime: VT Privacy of Consumer Financial and Health Information (Reg. IH-2001-01)
title: Opt-in authorization before disclosing consumer financial/health information (Vermont)
requirement: Insurance licensees must provide privacy notices and, because Vermont is an opt-in state, obtain the consumer's written or electronic authorization before disclosing nonpublic personal financial or health information to a nonaffiliated third party, subject to the regulation's exceptions. Pass condition: opt-in authorizations obtained and privacy notices delivered.
sourceNote: Verified on Vermont DFR Regulation IH-2001-01 (revised, effective June 20, 2023); opt-in state; in force July 2026.

regime: TX Insurance Consumer Health Information Privacy (28 TAC Ch. 22 Subch. B)
title: Opt-in authorization before disclosing nonpublic personal health information (Texas)
requirement: Insurers (covered entities) must obtain a valid opt-in authorization from the consumer before disclosing nonpublic personal health information, except as permitted, and may not unfairly discriminate against a consumer who declines to authorize disclosure. Pass condition: written authorizations obtained before any non-exempt health-information disclosure.
sourceNote: Verified on Texas Administrative Code Title 28, Chapter 22, Subchapter B (Insurance Consumer Health Information Privacy); opt-in health-info rule; in force July 2026.

regulatorName: Oregon Department of Justice (with DFR/insurance oversight)
title: OCPA consumer-data duties on insurers' non-GLBA data (no entity-level exemption)
requirement: Because the OCPA has only a data-level GLBA carve-out (no entity-level financial-institution exemption for insurers), an insurer acting as a controller over Oregon consumers' non-GLBA personal data must honor access/correction/deletion/opt-out rights, provide a privacy notice, obtain consent for sensitive data, and conduct data-protection assessments. Pass condition: OCPA controller obligations met for all non-GLBA personal data.
sourceNote: Verified via Oregon DOJ / ORS 646A.570-589; OCPA effective July 1, 2024, data-level GLBA exemption only; in force July 2026.

title: Governance & risk-management framework for use of external consumer data (Reg 10-1-1)
requirement: Life, private-passenger auto and health insurers using external consumer data and information sources, algorithms or predictive models must establish and document a cross-functional governance and risk-management framework covering design, testing, deployment and ongoing monitoring to prevent unfair discrimination against protected classes. Pass condition: documented framework maintained and available to the DOI.
sourceNote: Verified on Colorado SOS CCR / Justia; Reg 10-1-1 adopted effective Nov 14, 2023, amended effective Oct 15, 2025; in force July 2026.

title: Private-passenger auto ECDIS governance progress/compliance report to DOI
requirement: Private-passenger automobile insurers using external consumer data, algorithms or predictive models must submit a narrative progress report on their governance framework by Dec 1, 2025 and a compliance-summary report by July 1, 2026 and annually thereafter. Pass condition: reports filed with the Colorado DOI on schedule.
sourceNote: Verified on Colorado SOS CCR / Justia; auto amendment effective Dec 1, 2025 with narrative report Dec 1, 2025 and annual compliance report from July 1, 2026.

regulatorName: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
title: Written underwriting-guideline basis and adverse-action notice under N.J.A.C. 11:1-40
requirement: Insurers must maintain written, dated underwriting guidelines, furnish them to the Commissioner and to applicants on request, and on every declination or termination identify the specific guideline and factual basis relied upon; prohibited factors (race, gender, marital status, geography alone, etc.) may not be used. Pass condition: documented guideline basis cited on each adverse action.
sourceNote: Verified on New Jersey Administrative Code Title 11, Chapter 1, Subchapter 40; in force July 2026.

regulatorName: Arizona Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions
regime: Arizona Insurance Information and Privacy Protection (A.R.S. Title 20 Ch. 11)
title: Restriction on inquiring into prior adverse underwriting decisions (Arizona)
requirement: An insurance institution, producer or insurance-support organization may not seek information about an individual's previous adverse underwriting decision unless the inquiry also requests the reasons for that prior decision, and may not base a decision on the prior decision itself. Pass condition: underwriting inquiries and decisions comply with the prior-decision limitation.
sourceNote: Verified on Arizona Revised Statutes 20-2111; in force July 2026.
